Pakistan, US hold counterterrorism dialogue, reaffirm commitment to combating terrorist groups. WASHINGTON: The United States and Pakistan on Tuesday held the fourth counterterrorism dialogue in Washington, reaffirming their commitment to combating terrorist groups and strengthening security cooperation at a time when regional tensions remain high. The talks were led by US Coordinator for Counterterrorism Ambassador Gregory LoGerfo and Foreign Ministry Special Secretary Ambassador Nabeel Munir, a joint statement released by the US State Department said. “The dialogue underscored shared interests in the US-Pakistan counterterrorism partnership and the two countries’ determination to confront terrorism,” the joint statement said. “Delegations exchanged views on the current threat environment, explored avenues to enhance collaboration, and discussed steps to strengthen border security and disrupt terrorist facilitation networks,” it added. The statement specifically named ISIS-Khorasan (ISIS-K), Al Qaeda, the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), and the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and its affiliates among organisations that both governments said posed threats to regional security. “The US and Pakistan affirmed their joint resolve to confront terrorist organisations that endanger the safety of their citizens and the stability of the region,” the statement said. “The two governments committed to ensuring their counterterrorism collaboration to keep both of their nations safe and secure, and as part of an enduring vision of regional peace, prosperity, and stability,” it said. Meanwhile, the Foreign Office said that the two sides held “extensive deliberations on the regional and global terrorist threat and pledged to deepen counterterrorism collaboration both bilaterally and at multilateral fora”. The renewed engagement marks a shift from the difficult period in US-Pakistan relations following the withdrawal of American forces from Afghanistan in 2021. Washington had expressed concerns over terrorists sanctuaries in the region, while Islamabad repeatedly highlighted the security challenges it faced from cross-border militancy and instability in Afghanistan. In recent years, both countries have sought to focus on areas of mutual interest, including counterterrorism, trade, investment, climate cooperation, and regional stability. Pakistan’s strategic location and longstanding diplomatic links with neighbouring countries have also increased its importance in regional diplomacy. The country’s diplomatic role also gained renewed attention during the US-Iran conflict, as Islamabad has mediated between the two sides. The improved engagement with the US also comes as Pakistan continues to face serious internal security challenges . According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies , an Islamabad-based think tank, violence linked to terrorist attacks and counter-terrorism operations intensified sharply in July, making it the deadliest month of 2026, with 112 security personnel among 205 people killed. Pakistan, US look to finalise reciprocal trade framework While representatives from the US and Pakistan held counter-terrorism discussions in Washington, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb held a virtual meeting with United States Trade Representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer from Islamabad. The meeting was held to review the progress of ongoing negotiations, which are focused on strengthening bilateral trade and economic cooperation between Pakistan and the US, a statement released by the finance ministry said. The engagement took place roughly three weeks after the finance minister visited Washington , where he held talks with senior American officials on trade, tariffs, investment and economic cooperation. During his visit, Mr Aurangzeb held meetings with officials from the Office of the Trade Representative, the US Export-Import Bank (Exim), the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and the International Monetary Fund. The discussions focused on a possible bilateral trade agreement covering tariffs, market access, investment opportunities and wider economic cooperation. Separate talks with the Exim Bank and the DFC explored financing for infrastructure, energy and private-sector investment projects in Pakistan. During the meeting on Wednesday, he recalled his recent discussions in Washington and “welcomed the steady progress made by the respective negotiating teams and appreciated the constructive engagement that has characterised the dialogue over time”, the finance ministry said. It added that both sides noted that negotiations on the proposed reciprocal trade framework had advanced significantly and reaffirmed their shared commitment to conclude the agreement at the earliest. “The finance minister highlighted the importance of maintaining the momentum of negotiations in view of Pakistan’s economic priorities. “He emphasised that a strengthened trade and investment partnership with the United States would contribute to Pakistan’s export-led growth strategy, support economic resilience, and create greater commercial opportunities for businesses in both countries,” the statement read. It further said that Auragzeb also underlined the importance of continued collaboration with the Exim Bank to facilitate bilateral trade and investment. According to the finance ministry, Ambassador Greer acknowledged Pakistan’s continued engagement throughout the negotiations. He reaffirmed the United States’ commitment to “sustaining the positive trajectory of bilateral trade discussions and expressed confidence that the remaining issues could be resolved through continued technical engagement”, the finance ministry said. It added that Aurangzeb also emphasised the importance of maintaining close coordination and accelerating technical-level discussions to build on the progress already achieved. “Both sides expressed satisfaction with the progress achieved and agreed to continue working closely to finalise the remaining elements of the framework and agreed to continue regular engagement with a view to concluding the reciprocal trade framework soon, further strengthening the longstanding economic partnership between Pakistan and the United States,” the ministry’s statement read. It added that Greer also “appreciated the progress made on labour and regulatory reforms, including measures relating to forced labour compliance”. Pakistan is among the 60 countries on which the US imposed new import tariffs last month over what Washington said was their failure to effectively prohibit imports of goods produced with forced labour. Pakistan was placed in the lower 10 per cent tariff category, alongside countries that had either adopted forced labour import prohibitions, committed to doing so under reciprocal trade arrangements, or had partial enforcement regimes. The finance ministry said that Pakistan’s Federal Secretary for Commerce Jawad Paul and senior team members of the USTR also joined Wednesday’s meeting.

Two young women suspected of petty theft die in Lahore police custody. LAHORE: Two young women, suspected of stealing a small amount of cash and gold jewellery from a house, later died in the police custody under mysterious circumstances here on Tuesday. The women were brought to the Township police station when a local resident accused them of stealing money and gold ornaments from his house. However, one of them was later shifted to Lytton Road police station. As per initial reports, health condition of both women worsened in police custody owing to reasons yet to be ascertained. The suspects were shifted to different hospitals, where doctors declared them “received dead,” adding to the concern of police authorities as they were already facing an odd situation following the alleged rape of a mentally challenged girl by a police official inside a police station in Ghaziabad on Tuesday. DIG claims the suspects died of drug overdose The complainant, Zeeshan Latif, alleged in the FIR that the women entered his house and asked his wife for water. He said when his wife went to fetch water, the suspects stole her gold ornaments and Rs5,000 cash from the house. He said that as the women were caught red-handed, locals gathered there, thrashed them and then handed them over to the police. A spokesperson for the investigation police late on Tuesday made it clear that the women died in the custody of the operations wing police as was evident from the call made by them (officials of the operations wing) to the Rescue 1122 to shift them to hospitals. Operations DIG Faisal Kamran told Dawn that one of the suspects fainted in Township police station, while the other in Lytton Road police station. He said both women were immediately rushed to hospitals, where they were pronounced dead by the attending doctors. To a question, he said that the Township police had lodged an FIR against the suspects around 4:50pm. He said that one of the suspects was shifted to the Lytton Road police station, to hand her over to women police officials for further investigation, while the other was still in the custody of Township police. The DIG strongly denied the allegations that the women were tortured or treated harshly in custody. “As per initial inquiry reports, both were chronic drug addicts,” Kamran said, claiming the health condition of the women was compromised due to probable drug overdose, when they were handed over to the operations police. The incident still required a high level inquiry to dig out facts as the death of two women in custody must not be ignored under any circumstances, he added. He said the police officials are in contact with the doctors of the concerned hospitals in order to get the postmortem examination of the bodies conducted as soon as possible. To another question, the DIG said the police have obtained video clips showing the women after they were caught by the area residents. He said a video recording also showed one of the women being questioned by a police official. The video shows the woman asking the policeman to arrange narcotics for her, he added. The DIG said that more details would be shared with the media once investigations into the incident are finalised. Published in Dawn, August 5th, 2026

The viral videos that inspired tens of thousands to swim from Morocco to Spain’s Ceuta. Last week’s rush of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta began with a trickle. Encouraged by a handful of viral videos, ​including some posted by a Spanish news outlet intended to highlight the burden of migration pressures, the movement of a few dozen youths quickly turned into ‌tens of thousands swimming en masse by last Thursday. More than 80 people drowned or were crushed in a stampede, according to official tallies. A catalyst came three weeks earlier, when Spain’s Supreme Court published a ruling saying migrants caught at sea could not be immediately pushed back at the border of Spain’s North African territories of Ceuta and Melilla. The ruling does not preclude their summary return afterwards, legal experts said. View this post on Instagram Ceuta has long drawn ​migrants hoping to build a new life in Europe. But as misinterpretations of the ruling spread — including claims anyone who reached Ceuta, by sea or land, could not be ​returned — more and more people tried their luck. “Never believe those who tell you that if you get into Ceuta, they will send you ⁠back. You will not be sent back,” said a young Moroccan man filmed on a street in Germany in a video, which was deleted but later reposted by other accounts. Several posts ​on Meta’s platforms since July 7, including one with over 28,000 likes, also falsely claimed that Spain’s existing programme to regularise hundreds of thousands of illegal migrants would end on July 30. ​Similar messages circulated in the early hours of July 30. In fact, irregular migrants who had already been in Spain for at least five months before end-2025 could submit applications between April and June 30. The Spanish government received more than double the 500,000 registrations it had expected and never extended the deadline. Most videos and online groups amplifying the calls to rush to Ceuta have since been deleted and their original posting dates are unclear. ​In 2024, Morocco prosecuted scores of suspected online instigators of a foiled mass crossing. Unintended effect of Spanish media report By July 23, about 100 people had reached Ceuta, according to El Faro de ​Ceuta, a local news outlet that linked the arrivals to the Supreme Court decision, a view later echoed by Spanish and Moroccan officials, who accused human trafficking networks of propagating and exploiting such misinformation on social media. The ‌footage El Faro ⁠broadcast online of young men grinning and flashing thumbs-up and V-signs in Ceuta had the unintended effect of encouraging more people to attempt the crossing, according to migrants interviewed by Reuters . Hundreds began to swim across. Another spur came on July 28, when a new El Faro report with the caption “Ceuta can’t take it anymore” showed two grinning, waterlogged young women walking the city’s streets after making the crossing. The clip was widely viewed in Morocco, according to three migrants interviewed by Reuters . Influencers rush in The next day, social media was flooded with videos as influencers with tens of ​thousands of followers posted clips of themselves swimming ​to Ceuta, some with wetsuits and swim ⁠rings. Mounim Belhaj, a dog groomer with 31,000 Instagram followers, said he decided to go after seeing reports about migrants being housed at Ceuta’s reception centre. “Spanish media were showing good treatment of migrants arriving in Spain and that encouraged us a lot to go there,” he said. There were misleading ​videos, too. One, viewed millions of times, showed a young man with a selfie stick swimming toward what some posts identified as Ceuta, ​but had in fact been ⁠filmed in a city on Morocco’s Atlantic coast earlier in July. The next morning, the numbers surged. Spanish authorities said more than 70,000 people entered Ceuta irregularly. Chat groups also appear to have played a role. A report by Spanish security analyst Chema Gil identified two public WhatsApp groups administered by Algerian phone numbers, with a total of 3,700 members, providing advice on routes to Ceuta. The chats urged members ⁠to move quickly, ​with messages such as, “Those who do not move today will regret it tomorrow.” Gil could not identify the administrators ​and Reuters was unable to independently verify the groups, which have since been deleted. By the next evening, hunger and hostility had driven the vast majority to go back. Thousands remain stranded, particularly sub-Saharan Africans and unaccompanied minors who cannot be ​deported. “We made a mistake in going there,” Belhaj said. “There was only hunger.”

Youm-i-Istehsal: Pakistan says lasting peace in South Asia linked to peaceful resolution of Kashmir dispute. The military and civilian leadership on Wednesday said just and lasting peace in South Asia was closely linked to the peaceful resolution of the Kashmir dispute as the country marked Youm-i-Istehsal (Exploitation Day) to mark the anniversary of India revoking the occupied region’s special autonomy in 2019. President Asif Ali Zardari said that Youm-i-Istehsal was being observed to “reaffirm our unwavering solidarity” with the people of occupied Kashmir. “We pay tribute to their courage, resilience and commitment to their just struggle for the realisation of their inalienable right to self-determination,” he said. The president said that seven years have passed since India’s “illegal and unilateral actions” of August 5, 2019, when it revoked the region’s special autonomy. “These actions cannot change the legal status of the dispute, nor can they weaken the resolve of the Kashmiri people,” he said. “For seven years, millions of Kashmiris have continued to live under severe restrictions that have affected every aspect of daily life. Families have endured uncertainty, young people have seen their opportunities constrained and entire communities have continued to bear the burden of prolonged conflict and instability. Despite these hardships, the people of Jammu and Kashmir have remained steadfast in their pursuit of justice and their legitimate right to determine their own future,” President Zardari said. He said that Pakistan remained unwavering in its moral, political and diplomatic support for the people of occupied Kashmir. “We will continue to raise our voice at every international forum until the Jammu and Kashmir dispute is resolved in accordance with the relevant United Nations Security Council (UNSC) resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people,” he said. The president said that just and lasting peace in South Asia was closely linked to the peaceful resolution of Kashmir dispute, urging the international community to play its role in addressing the human rights situation in the occupied valley. “To my Kashmiri brothers and sisters, I say: Pakistan stands firmly with you. Your courage in the face of adversity inspires us. You are not alone. The people of Pakistan will continue to stand by you until your legitimate right to self-determination is realised,” he said. In his message, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the people and the government of Pakistan “stand in unwavering solidarity with our Kashmiri brothers and sisters”. He said that seven years later, India’s unlawful measures had neither changed the legal status of occupied Kashmir nor diminished the legitimate aspiration of its people. “Instead, they have deepened repression, undermined fundamental freedom, and accelerated attempts to alter the demographic composition of the occupied territory through unlawful legislative and administrative measures. The continued suppression of the genuine Kashmiri political leadership, restrictions on civil liberties, and curbs on independent media, remain a matter of serious concern,” he said. “Despite these challenges, the courage, resilience and steadfastness of the Kashmiri people remain unshaken. Their peaceful and just struggle for the realization of their unalienable right to self-determination continues to inspire generations and commands the respect and support of all those who believe in justice, human dignity and the rule of international law,” he added. The premier said that the Kashmir dispute remained the “principal unresolved issue affecting peace and stability in South Asia”. “Lasting peace in the region cannot be achieved by coercion or unilateral action, but only through a peaceful settlement of the dispute in accordance with the aspirations of the Kashmiri people and the relevant UNSC resolutions. The international community must move beyond expressions of concern and play its rightful role in advancing a just and durable resolution of the dispute,” he said. He reaffirmed that a peaceful and just resolution of the dispute remained a cornerstone of Pakistan’s foreign policy, adding that Pakistan would continue to “extend its diplomatic, political and moral support and raise the voice of the Kashmiri people at every regional and international forum”. PM Shehbaz said that Pakistan called upon the international community to urge India to end its human rights violations in occupied Kashmir, reverse its “illegal and unilateral measures” introduced since August 2019, repeal the draconian laws imposed upon the people and create conducive environment to enable the peaceful resolution of the Kashmir dispute, through the exercise of the right to self-determination by the Kashmiri people in accordance with the relevant UNSC resolutions. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, in his message on the occasion, called on the international community to fulfil its “long-overdue responsibility” for the peaceful resolution of the dispute. DPM Dar said India’s actions in occupied Kashmir on August 5, 2019, presented a “grave challenge” to the established international framework and expressed solidarity with the people of the region. “We reaffirm our unwavering support for their fundamental rights, as enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations and reflected in the relevant UNSC resolutions,” he said, adding that events of August 5, 2019 remained a “matter of deep concern”. He continued: “These steps have further complicated efforts to promote peace and stability in South Asia and have adversely impacted the lives, rights, and freedoms of the Kashmiri people.” At this, the DPM urged the international community to play a role in ensuring respect for international law, international humanitarian law, human rights and commitments made under the UN. Dar also called on India to halt all actions aimed at undermining the disputed status of occupied Kashmir and “take steps conducive to creating an environment for the peaceful resolution of the dispute”. “We reiterate that lasting peace and stability in South Asia can only be achieved through the resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with the aspirations of the Kashmiri people and the relevant UNSC resolutions,” he said, adding that Pakistan will continue to raise its voice on international forums for a “just and peaceful settlement of the dispute”. Concluding his statement, Dar paid tribute to the “resilience, courage, and sacrifices” of the Kashmiri people. “Pakistan stands in steadfast solidarity with them and will continue to extend its unwavering moral, political, and diplomatic support to their just struggle for the realisation of their legitimate right to self- determination.” He called upon the international community, particularly the UN, to “fulfil its long-overdue responsibilities and make meaningful efforts for a peaceful resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute”. Separately, foreign ministry officials, led by the foreign secretary, participated in a solidarity walk on Islamabad’s Constitution Avenue to “reaffirm Pakistan’s unwavering support for the Kashmiri people”, a statement on the ministry’s X said. It said Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam addressed the rally and reiterated Pakistan’s “steadfast political, diplomatic and moral support for the just struggle of the Kashmiri people and their inalienable right to self-determination, in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions and Organisation of Islamic Cooperation resolutions”. Armed forces reaffirm solidarity with Kashmiris Separately, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf and Chief of Air Staff Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu reaffirm their unwavering solidarity with the resilient and courageous people of occupied Kashmir. A statement issued by Inter-Services Public Relations said, “The armed forces of Pakistan reiterate their steadfast support for the legitimate struggle of Kashmiri people to exercise their inalienable right to self-determination as enshrined in international law and the relevant UNSC resolutions.” They said that the continued occupation of the valley remained a matter of “serious concern”. “Such actions, coupled with provocative rhetoric and belligerent posturing, serve only to exacerbate regional instability and perpetuate human suffering,” they said. “It is explicitly evident that lasting peace and stability in South Asia are intrinsically linked to the just and peaceful settlement of Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with aspirations of the Kashmiri people and the relevant UNSC resolutions,” they added.

House commends Korean envoy for strengthening Philippines-Korea strategic ties. A measure commending outgoing Korean Ambassador Lee Sang-hwa for strengthening relations between the Philippines and South Korea has been adopted in the House of Representatives. Adopted via simple voice vote (ayes vs. nayes) during plenary session Tuesday, Aug. 4 was House Resolution (HR) No. 1275. It was filed by Speaker Isabela 6th district Rep. Faustino “Bojie” Dy III, Majority Leader Ilocos Norte 1st district Sandro Marcos, and Minority Leader 4Ps Party-list Rep. Marcelino "Nonoy" Libanan. "President Ferdinand ‘Bongbong’ Marcos Jr. recognized Ambassador Lee’s distinguished service through the Order of Sikatuna, and under Speaker Bojie Dy, the House is adding the voice of the Filipino people to that expression of gratitude. His tenure helped move our partnership toward deeper cooperation in security, agriculture, energy and trade,” Rep. Marcos said. HR No. 1275 honors Lee following the completion of his three-year tour of duty as ambassador to the Philippines on July 9, 2026. The measure takes cognizance of President Marcos’ conferment on Lee of the Order of Sikatuna with the Rank of Datu, Grand Cross, Gold Distinction. The Order of Sikatuna is the country’s diplomatic order of merit for individuals who have rendered exceptional service to the Philippines and strengthened friendship between nations. The resolution recalls that the Philippines became the first Southeast Asian country to establish diplomatic relations with South Korea on March 3, 1949. It also recognizes the shared sacrifices of Filipinos and Koreans during the Korean War in defense of freedom and democratic principles. The measure credits Lee’s stewardship for the formal elevation of bilateral ties into a strategic partnership through the Joint Declaration signed on Oct. 7, 2024. “Stronger relations with South Korea can help Filipino farmers gain better technology, support more reliable energy, generate investments and improve our country’s security capabilities. These are areas of cooperation that can create lasting benefits for ordinary families,” added the majority leader and presidential son. The strategic partnership gave effect to 10 bilateral agreements covering defense procurement, agricultural modernization and nuclear energy infrastructure. The resolution also recognizes expanded cooperation in security, trade, cultural exchanges and efforts to address regional and global challenges. The House expressed support for President Marcos’ recognition of Lee and affirmed the value the Philippines places on its historic alliance and continuing partnership with South Korea. Copies of the resolution will be transmitted to Lee and the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Manila.

Bulacan healthcare gets major boost with advanced heart tech. The Provincial Government of Bulacan has equipped the Emilio G. Perez Memorial District Hospital (EGPMDH) in Hagonoy with a state of the art 2D Echo Ultrasound Machine with Doppler, courtesy of the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO). This advanced cardiovascular diagnostic tool allows doctors to perform echocardiography with Doppler imaging, a procedure that provides real time visualization of the heart’s chambers, valves, and blood flow. It can detect abnormalities such as valve defects, heart enlargement, and irregular circulation—conditions that often require early intervention to prevent life threatening complications. By bringing this technology directly to the first district, coastal residents no longer need to travel to distant hospitals or pay high fees at private facilities for essential heart screening and monitoring. The machine significantly boosts EGPMDH’s capacity to deliver specialized cardiac care at the community level. Alongside the turnover, PCSO also released ₱1.8 million representing Bulacan’s Lotto revenue share for the first half of the year, in line with Executive Order No. 357 A, which mandates the allocation of Lotto revenues to local government units for health and social programs. Bulacan Governor Daniel R. Fernando expressed gratitude to PCSO, stressing that modernizing district hospitals with cutting edge equipment is central to his administration’s vision of equal access to quality healthcare for all Bulakenyos.

Biazon warns Muntinlupa employees who violate the law. Muntinlupa Mayor Ruffy Biazon gave an ultimatum to city government employees that they will face dismissal from the service if they break the law. “Walang puwang ang pasaway sa Pamahalaang Lungsod. Magsilbi sana itong last warning sa sinumang empleyado ng City Government na lalabag sa batas: Hindi ko na kayo ipapatawag. Sa susunod, pauuwiin ko na lang kayo (There is no room for disobedient [employees] in the City Government. I hope this will serve as a last warning to any City Government employee who violates the law: I will no longer summon you. Next time, I will just send you home),” he said. Biazon’s warning came after several law violations of city government employees were posted on social media. One employee was caught riding a motorcycle without a helmet. They were summoned to the mayor’s office but he said it was tiring to repeatedly chastise them before they comply. “It is not tolerable anymore. Hindi puwedeng tayo ang nagpapatupad ng batas pero tayo rin ang unang lumalabag. Nawawalan tayo ng kredibilidad bilang law enforcers at bilang public servants (We cannot be the ones enforcing the law but we are also the first to violate it. We are losing credibility as law enforcers and as public servants),” said Biazon. He advised employees to stay away from acts that will tarnish the image of the city government, saying discipline and accountability should start from them.

COA witness says guidelines silent on aliases for intel agents, informants. Former Commission on Audit (COA) Intelligence and Confidential Fund Audit Office (ICFAO) State Auditor Atty. Roderick Wamil told the impeachment court on Wednesday that the guidelines governing confidential and intelligence funds do not explicitly allow or prohibit the use of aliases for intelligence agents or informants. Testifying during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, Wamil said the COA-Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Joint Circular No. 2015-01 is "silent" on whether fictitious names or aliases may be used in documents supporting confidential fund disbursements. His testimony came after Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo asked whether the circular required the disclosure of the actual identities of intelligence agents or informants who allegedly received confidential funds from the Office of the Vice President (OVP), citing names such as "Mary Grace Piattos," "Chippy McDonald," and "Mickey Mouse." Wamil replied that the circular contains no provision on the matter. "It is neither allowed nor prohibited," he said when Tulfo asked whether the absence of a specific rule meant the practice was permissible. Tulfo then questioned why COA auditors did not seek to determine the true identities of the listed recipients during the audit of the OVP's confidential funds. Wamil explained that the audit conducted by the ICFAO was a compliance audit, with auditors determining only whether the documents complied with the requirements set out in the joint circular. "Our audit is a compliance audit. Whatever is provided in the circular serves as the basis of our audit," he said. Later, Senator-judge Bam Aquino also questioned Wamil on the issue, asking whether previous COA guidelines had ever expressly allowed the use of code names or aliases. Wamil said that, based on his recollection, even earlier circulars in effect during his time at the ICFAO did not contain any provision addressing aliases. Aquino then asked whether COA expected the names appearing in supporting documents to belong to actual persons. Wamil said the audit process is document-based, and auditors have no way of independently determining whether a listed name is an alias. However, when Aquino asked if the expectation is that documents submitted to COA identify real individuals, Wamil replied in the affirmative. The exchange formed part of the impeachment court's examination of the liquidation and auditing procedures for the OVP's confidential funds, an issue central to one of the articles of impeachment against Duterte.

Japan and Southeast Asia: Trust and Strengthening People-to-People Exchanges. By YUSUKE UMEZAKI Relations between Japan and Southeast Asia are growing ever closer. People-to-people exchanges, including tourism, are becoming increasingly active, while interest in each other’s cultures continues to grow. Through post World War II reconciliation and decades of cooperation, Japan and Southeast Asia have steadily deepened mutual trust, and their ties are now entering a new phase. Southeast Asia festivals draw large crowds More than 280,000 people attended Thai Festival Tokyo 2026, held over two days in May at Yoyogi Park in Shibuya Ward, Tokyo.First held in 2000, the festival celebrated its 26th edition this year. Visitors enjoyed authentic Thai cuisine, including hoy tod (Thai-style oyster omelet) and pad thai, as well as the opportunity to experience muay thai and watch traditional dance performances. One of the festival’s biggest attractions was a T-pop stage featuring popular Thai artists and actors, which drew such large crowds that entry had to be temporarily restricted. Some fans even traveled from as far as Osaka, western Japan, to see the popular actor duo TayNew. Vorapong Vadhanasindhu, Counsellor at the Royal Thai Embassy in Tokyo, noted that a growing number of Japanese people are becoming interested in Thai entertainment, including T-pop and television dramas. With the 140th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Japan and Thailand approaching in 2027, he expressed hope for further strengthening ties between the two countries. At Laos Festival 2026, also held at Yoyogi Park in May, Japan's Princess Aiko, the eldest daughter of Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako, attended the opening ceremony. Dressed in a light green traditional Lao costume presented by the Lao side, she watched a welcoming dance performed by the Laotian National Dance and Music Troupe on the park’s outdoor stage before joining Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Thongsavan Phomvihane and other dignitaries for the ribbon-cutting ceremony. Similar festivals celebrating countries across Southeast Asia, including the Philippines, Indonesia, and Vietnam, are held in Tokyo each year, and all draw large crowds. Visitors to Japan increase tenfold The number of visitors from Southeast Asia to Japan is also on the rise. According to the Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO), 42,683,837 foreign visitors traveled to Japan in 2025. Of these, 4,800,123 came from six major member states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)--Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam--accounting for 11.2% of the total. Compared with the 441,602 visitors recorded in 2003, when the Japanese government launched the Visit Japan campaign, the number has increased more than tenfold in just over two decades. According to a 2026 survey conducted across ASEAN by the Singapore-based think tank ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute, Japan ranked first among respondents’ preferred holiday destinations, with 32.5% selecting Japan. This was well ahead of ASEAN member states (13.4%), European Union (EU) member states (9.7%), and Australia (9.4%), demonstrating Japan’s overwhelming popularity as a holiday destination. High levels of trust In the same survey, 65.6% of respondents said they trusted Japan, making it the most trusted among the five countries and regions surveyed—Japan, the United States, China, India, and the European Union (EU)—for the eighth consecutive year. By comparison, the figures for the United States and China were 44.0% and 39.8%, respectively. When asked why they trusted Japan, 41.4% of respondents cited its status as ”a responsible stakeholder that respects and champions international law.” An additional 22.7% pointed to its "vast economic resources and the political will to provide global leadership." Meanwhile, only 15.7% said they did not trust Japan, the lowest percentage among the five countries and regions surveyed. Friendship over division Japan has not always enjoyed a positive image in Southeast Asia. During World War II, Japan invaded countries across Asia. Even after the war, anti-Japanese sentiment remained strong in the region. Against this backdrop, Japan worked to rebuild its relationships through war reparations, economic cooperation, and other efforts. “There have been times in the past when our relationship has faced arduous time,” Emperor Naruhito noted at a state banquet held in late May in honor of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. during the president’s state visit to Japan. He went on to say that “since the normalization of diplomatic relations in 1956, Japan and the Philippines have moved forward hand in hand, strengthening our relationship one step at a time to establish the firm friendship we enjoy today.” In his response, President Marcos said that the ties between the two countries had been built by “generations of Filipinos and Japanese who chose understanding over difference, friendship over division, and partnership over isolation.” As Japan and the Philippines marked the 70th anniversary of the normalization of diplomatic relations in July, President Marcos described the current state of bilateral ties as being in a “platinum age” during talks with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Tokyo. The term took the “golden age” that President Marcos had used during then Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba’s visit to Manila in April 2025 a step further. Today, the two countries’ ties have been elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. A pledge made half a century ago The turning point in relations between Japan and Southeast Asia can be traced back to the Fukuda Doctrine, a diplomatic policy announced half a century ago. In August 1977, then Japanese Prime Minister Takeo Fukuda toured Southeast Asia, visiting Malaysia, Indonesia, and other countries. At the final stop on his tour in Manila, he delivered a speech on relations between Japan and Southeast Asia. At the time, the president of the Philippines was Ferdinand Marcos Sr., the father of the current president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Fukuda rejected a return to Japanese militarism while positioning Japan as “an equal partner” of Southeast Asia. He also stressed that “it is not enough for our relationship to be based solely on mutual material and economic benefit,” adding that “heart-to-heart” understanding between the two sides were essential. The principles of the Fukuda Doctrine continue to guide relations between Japan and Southeast Asia. In 2027, the doctrine will mark the 50th anniversary. As the international landscape continues to evolve, there is hope that Japan and Southeast Asia will further deepen people-to-people exchanges and carry the doctrine’s principles into the next generation.

D&L sees higher consumer spending, lower coconut oil prices boosting H2 performance. D&L Industries Inc. expects an even stronger second half after posting higher profits in the first half of 2026, driven by improved second-quarter performance amid recovering consumer spending and lower coconut oil prices. In a media briefing on Wednesday, Aug. 5, D&L President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Alvin D. Lao said, “In the last couple of weeks, the traffic seems to have returned. There are a lot of people in restaurants and malls. So, it seems like it [consumer spending] is coming back a little. So, that’s a sign. It looks like the consumer economy and our food ingredients business as well is getting better.” “Meanwhile, the gradual normalization of coconut oil prices is a welcome development. Our food ingredients business delivered a significant turnaround in the second quarter of 2026, which we believe signals that earnings have likely bottomed and reached an inflection point. As raw material costs stabilize and our portfolio optimization initiatives continue to gain traction, we are optimistic about the segment’s ability to deliver more stable and improved profitability moving forward,” he added. Lao noted, “2026 has remained a challenging year thus far, marked by geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, elevated inflation, and higher interest rates. Despite these headwinds, the company was able to grow its earnings by eight percent in the first half of the year.” “Overall, we remain confident in the long-term prospects of the business. While prevailing macroeconomic uncertainties continue to weigh on market valuations and liquidity, they have also created opportunities to acquire high-quality businesses at attractive valuations,” he said, noting that the Lao family’s investment arm, Jadel Holdings Co. Inc., has increased its stake in D&L by approximately 4.4 percent since the pandemic. At current levels, the stock continues to offer an attractive dividend yield of approximately 6.7 percent and, based on current performance, Lao said the company will be able to sustain dividends equivalent to 65 percent of the previous year’s net income, consisting of a 50-percent regular dividend and a 15-percent special dividend. D&L reported an eight-percent increase in net income to ₱1.5 billion for the first half of 2026, with second-quarter profit rising 10 percent year-on-year to ₱786 million despite the challenges posed by the Iran war. “With coconut oil—one of our key raw materials—stabilizing at around $2,100 per metric ton (MT) after a prolonged period of volatility, margins continued to recover in the first half of 2026. The recovery was particularly evident in the high margin specialty products (HMSP) segment, where gross profit margins (GPM) expanded by 2.1 percentage points (ppts) during the period, reflecting easing input cost pressures alongside continued price pass-through,” Lao explained. Meanwhile, the sales mix shifted modestly back toward HMSP, which accounted for 51 percent of revenues in the first half of 2026. As the company continues to allocate a significant portion of its resources toward developing HMSP, management expects HMSP to account for an increasingly larger share of the sales mix over time. Meanwhile, D&L’s specialty plastics segment continued to deliver a solid performance, with earnings increasing 24 percent year-on-year, driven by 27-percent volume growth and a 0.3-ppt expansion in gross margins. Consumer products original design manufacturer (ODM) also continued to deliver strong growth, with earnings increasing 27 percent year-on-year, driven by seven-percent volume growth as the plant in Batangas province continued to ramp up. Export sales now account for 19 percent of total segment revenues, up from virtually zero five years ago, highlighting the company’s successful execution in expanding its presence in international markets.

The toxic afterlife of e-waste and the hidden cost of digital progress. Have you ever wondered where the phone, laptop, refrigerator, or charger you dispose of goes after you discard it? Some are brought to recycling centers, while others end up in landfills as electronic waste, or e-waste. Still others are transported from different parts of the world disguised as donations or recyclable materials, only to end up as hazardous waste in countries like the Philippines. The Philippine News Agency reported that environmental groups estimate more than 200 containers of suspected e-waste have arrived in the country. The Bureau of Customs recently convened government agencies to discuss their respective roles in investigating and managing these shipments. Authorities are also looking into suspected processing activities inside the free port, including allegations that some establishments discarded residual materials that may harm the environment. Additionally, the health and welfare of workers who handle e-waste, as well as people in nearby communities, are at risk. The problem has long been a global challenge. The World Health Organization reported that only 22 percent of the 62 million metric tons of e-waste generated worldwide has been formally collected and recycled. The gap between what the world consumes and what it safely recovers continues to widen. E-waste is particularly dangerous because it contains both valuable and hazardous materials. Gold, copper, silver, palladium, and rare earth elements make discarded electronics attractive to recyclers. At the same time, these devices may also contain lead, mercury, cadmium, nickel, brominated flame retardants, acids, plastics, and battery chemicals. This is where proper e-waste management becomes critical. Modern facilities can recover valuable materials while protecting human health and the environment. However, poorly equipped junk shops and informal recycling operations can become toxic processing sites. The danger begins with unsafe dismantling. Informal recyclers may smash screens, strip wires, burn plastic coatings, heat circuit boards, dissolve metals in acid, or dump unwanted components into waterways and vacant lots. These practices release toxic substances into the air, soil, dust, and water. Lead and cadmium can contaminate soil and groundwater. Mercury can move through ecosystems and accumulate in fish. Burning plastics and insulated wires releases dioxins, furans, and fine particles. Over time, the pollution spreads beyond the recycling sites, affecting farms, rivers, drainage systems, and nearby communities. Many workers dismantling e-waste do not have adequate protective equipment. Some work without gloves, masks, proper ventilation, or training. They inhale toxic fumes, come into contact with contaminated dust, and unknowingly bring pollutants home on their clothing and skin. Children are especially vulnerable because they breathe more air, drink more water, and consume more food relative to their body weight than adults. Their brains and bodies are also developing. Pregnant women likewise face greater risks because some toxic substances can cross the placenta and affect the fetus. Exposure to e-waste pollution has been linked to respiratory irritation, reduced lung function, skin disorders, headaches, and increased risks to neurological development. Lead can damage the brain and nervous system. Mercury can impair coordination and development. Cadmium – a toxic, naturally occurring heavy metal widely used in rechargeable batteries, solar cells, and other products—can damage the kidneys and bones. Brominated flame retardants and other persistent chemicals can disrupt hormones and remain in the environment for years. The danger is not limited to workers. Families living near dumpsites or informal recycling areas may also be exposed through contaminated dust, food, water, and smoke. When e-waste remains inside shipping containers for extended periods, the risks increase. Batteries can degrade, swell, leak, or even ignite, especially under hot and humid conditions. Damaged screens, lamps, and electronic components can release hazardous residues. Corrosion may spread through mixed loads, making material recovery more difficult and increasing the risk of chemical exposure once containers are opened. Moisture can also damage equipment that might otherwise have been reused, turning potentially repairable electronics into hazardous waste. If importers abandon these shipments, port authorities and local communities may ultimately bear both the environmental risk and the cost of disposal. Globally, the movement of e-waste between nations, particularly from developed to developing countries, is regulated by agreements such as the Basel Convention. The treaty seeks to protect human health and the environment from hazardous waste, including discarded electronics and plastics. A 2025 amendment expanded controls over cross-border shipments of electrical and electronic waste and scrap, including materials intended for recycling. These measures make it more difficult to disguise hazardous shipments under vague labels. Still, laws are only as effective as the inspections, documentation systems, and penalties that enforce them. Solutions must begin long before a device becomes waste. Manufacturers should design electronics that last longer, are easier to repair, and use safer materials that reduce risks to workers who eventually dismantle them. Producers should also take greater responsibility for batteries, chargers, and accessories, which often fall outside existing collection systems. Consumers likewise have an important role. They can repair devices instead of replacing them prematurely, purchase durable products, return used electronics through verified collection programs, and avoid storing broken gadgets indefinitely. Schools, offices, and households should choose certified recyclers and ask where their discarded electronics go after collection. E-waste reveals one of the hidden costs of digital progress. The devices that connect, entertain, and power modern life should not become a threat to human health and the environment once they reach the end of their useful lives.

Taxi driver stabbed with screwdriver over pedestrian graze in QC. A taxi driver was stabbed twice with a screwdriver after his vehicle accidentally grazed a man walking along Gen. Luis Street in Barangay Nagkaisang Nayon, Novaliches, Quezon City, Monday afternoon, Aug. 3. Police said the driver pulled over after the minor contact and tried to talk to the man, identified only as alias “Mar-mar,” 45. The contact was minor and did not cause the man to fall, police said. However, when the driver opened his taxi window, the suspect, who was allegedly under the influence of liquor, suddenly stabbed him twice in the left side of his chest using a screwdriver. The incident happened at around 5:30 p.m. in front of ACCUPLUS along Gen. Luis Street. Personnel of the Quezon City Police District’s District Mobile Force Battalion (DMFB), who were conducting police visibility operations nearby, saw the attack and immediately arrested the suspect. Police recovered a 12-inch screwdriver allegedly used in the stabbing. The injured driver was rushed to East Avenue Medical Center for treatment. The suspect is facing a complaint for frustrated homicide before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office.

6.4-magnitude earthquake hits Davao Occidental — Phivolcs. A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck off the coast of Sarangani, Davao Occidental, at 12:14 p.m. on Wednesday, Aug. 5, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) said. In its Earthquake Information No. 2, Phivolcs revised the earthquake's magnitude from the initial estimate of 7.0 to 6.4 following further analysis. Phivolcs said the quake's epicenter was located 37 kilometers southwest of Balut Island in the municipality of Sarangani, Davao Occidental province, at a depth of 13 kilometers. It was tectonic in origin. Phivolcs said Intensity V, or strong shaking, was felt in Glan, Sarangani. Intensity IV (moderately strong) was recorded in Kiamba, Sarangani; General Santos City; Malungon and Alabel in Sarangani; and Tupi and Polomolok in South Cotabato. Intensity III (weak) was reported in Maasim, Maitum, and Malapatan in Sarangani; and Lake Sebu and Tampakan in South Cotabato. Intensity II or “slightly felt” shaking was reported in Koronadal City, Banga, and Surallah in South Cotabato. Based on instrumental observations, Intensity V was also recorded in Sarangani, Davao Occidental, and General Santos City. Phivolcs said no damage is expected from the earthquake, although aftershocks may occur.
