Radenta Technologies receive ISO Certification. Radenta Technologies, one of the country’s premiere solutions integrators, recently received its first ISO/IEC 27001 certification from the International Organization for Standardization. ISO/IEC 27001 is the world's leading standard for Information Security Management Systems (ISMS), providing a framework for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving information security. The Certification shows that an organization has implemented a systematic approach to protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the information it owns, processes, or manages through the integration of people, processes, policies, and technology. The scope includes the Provision of Information Security Management for the delivery of services for customized IT solutions associated with Cloud, Software Development, Project Management, and Systems Integration. “It is the time for Radenta to demonstrate that it is strongly committed to protecting client data,” remarks Nereo Bolante, Co-Director, Radenta Ethics, Compliance, and Governance Team (ECG). “Achieving this certification strengthens Radenta’s competitive advantage, particularly in government, healthcare, financial services, and other regulated industries. It also enhances our ability to manage security risks, improve operational resilience, and foster a strong security culture across the organization.” The certification proves that information security is embedded in the way Radenta operates. It is not just a badge or a marketing claim. This gives existing and future clients greater trust and confidence in doing business with the company. Clients are assured that their information is protected using internationally recognized security standards and industry best practices. Radenta Technologies has been at the forefront of the digital industry for almost a decade. It has a long roster of satisfied clients from a large swatch of the business landscape. It has fostered partnerships with government agencies. It launched its very own Radenta Academy in partnership with the Technical Educations and Skills Development Agency (TESDA) and is at present aggressively pushing for local government units to adapt AEGIS, the latest AI-enabled disaster management system developed by global award-winning technology firm Vantiq. Bolante adds, “Radenta will continue to strengthen its information security through continuous risk management, employee awareness, regular audits, enhanced cybersecurity controls, robust supplier governance, and alignment with evolving industry standards. Achieving ISO/IEC 27001 is not the finish line—it challenges us to continuously improve.”

No tsunami threat to Philippines after 6.4-magnitude Sarangani quake, says Phivolcs. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) on Wednesday, Aug. 5, assured the public that there is no tsunami threat to the Philippines following the magnitude 6.4 earthquake that struck off Sarangani, Davao Occidental. “No destructive tsunami threat exists based on available data,” Phivolcs said in a tsunami information bulletin. “This is for information purposes only and there is no tsunami threat to the Philippines from this earthquake,” it added. The earthquake occurred at 12:14 p.m., with its epicenter located 37 kilometers southwest of Sarangani, Davao Occidental, at a depth of 13 kilometers.

Manila council at 125 faces push for faster, more relevant laws. As it marked its 125th year on Tuesday, Aug. 4, the Manila City Council faced renewed calls from city leaders to pass more responsive legislation and strengthen coordination with the executive branch to better address residents’ needs. Manila Mayor Francisco "Isko Moreno" Domagoso and Vice Mayor Chi Atienza led the anniversary rites, which highlighted both the council’s long history and the expectations placed on it moving forward. The event opened with a Thanksgiving Mass at the Session Hall, followed by the unveiling of a civic heritage exhibit at Bulwagang Rodriguez. The display featured legislative records, landmark ordinances, and archival photographs tracing the council’s role in shaping city governance. Atienza emphasized the need for stronger collaboration between the legislative and executive branches, saying closer coordination allows policies and programs to be implemented more efficiently and felt more directly by Manileños. She also stressed the importance of building a lasting institutional legacy through meaningful legislation. Domagoso, for his part, urged councilors to prioritize measures that would have long-term impact, reminding them that their mandate ultimately lies with the public. He noted that effective governance depends on alignment between the city council and the executive branch, particularly in addressing everyday concerns and basic services. Beyond the formal program, city officials and employees joined an anniversary parade inside City Hall, while council offices hosted visitors and staff. The celebration concluded with a boodle fight at the Session Hall Lounge. While the milestone commemorates more than a century of lawmaking, officials acknowledged that the challenge remains in ensuring that legislation keeps pace with the evolving needs of Manila’s residents.

Afghanistan's child deaths are rising as food distributions face cuts - UN. ROME (AP) — Child malnutrition has reached critical levels in a third of Afghanistan’s provinces and is expected to worsen as funding shortfalls force cuts in food distributions and other support, the U.N. World Food Program said Tuesday. “We must act now to stem the rise in child deaths, which this crisis is provoking,” John Aylieff, WFP’s country director in Afghanistan, said in a statement, adding that “it is already too late for too many." Afghanistan continues to recover from decades of conflict and upheaval, including the chaotic withdrawal of U.S. forces in 2021 as the Taliban took power. Olga Cherevko, spokesperson for the U.N. humanitarian office in Afghanistan, said nutrition specialists report that “wasting among children has worsened this year in over three-quarters of the country." Children suffering from a condition known as wasting are acutely malnourished, become very thin for their height, and need immediate therapeutic feeding. But “too many children arrive at health facilities severely malnourished” while others never make it, Cherevko told reporters at U.N. headquarters by video from Afghanistan, where she has traveled across the country in recent months and weeks. WFP said 142 health centers closed in 2025 because of aid reductions and more than 13,000 children lost access to nutrition treatment. It did not mention any specific donor, such as the United States, where the Trump administration has made sweeping cuts in foreign aid. Nearly 3.7 million Afghan children are projected to suffer from acute malnutrition this year, along with 1.2 million pregnant and breastfeeding women, according to WFP. The agency said 12 Afghan provinces have reached critical levels of acute child malnutrition, a record number. It cited a combination of conflict, unemployment, rising food prices, disease outbreaks, poor water and sanitation and reduced humanitarian funding. The Iran war and other fighting have delayed deliveries WFP said supply shortages linked to conflict in the Middle East and the nine-month closure of Pakistan’s border because of fighting between the neighbors have disrupted deliveries of nutrition products, leaving nearly one million malnourished women and children without essential nutrition services for five months. From August through October, WFP said food distributions aimed at preventing famine in the worst-hit areas are being suspended due to lack of funding, even though the annual peak season for malnutrition is between July and October. It said it urgently needs $540 million over the next six months. WFP previously described cuts as ‘devastating’ Humanitarian groups in Afghanistan are grappling with steep funding cuts. In February, Aylieff told The Associated Press that cuts had been “devastating” and were forcing the agency to turn away three out of four acutely malnourished children. Funding for food assistance has dropped sharply — by about 59% since 2022 — even as needs have surged, according to a recent WFP report. In June, the U.S. pledged $800 million to WFP, which said it will help more than 38 million people in at least 37 countries. Cherevko of the U.N. humanitarian office said the larger $1.71 billion humanitarian appeal for Afghanistan is just over 26% funded, which is “alarming,” especially since malnutrition and other indicators are worsening.

Danube River's water is dropping so low that World War II ships are emerging. PRAHOVO, Serbia (AP) — Water levels on the Danube River, the second longest in Europe, have dropped so low because of drought that the hulks of dozens of World War II German battleships are emerging into view. They are a curious distraction from the summer heat crisis. The Danube’s record low water levels also have forced power plants to the brink of shutting down, and governments across Central and Eastern Europe are taking steps to conserve electricity. In the middle of the river separating Serbia and Romania near the Serbian port of Prahovo, a rusty hull is now visible along with a broken mast where the Nazi flag used to fly. The ships, some still laden with weapons, belonged to Nazi Germany’s Black Sea fleet that the Germans deliberately sank as they retreated from Romania and as Soviet forces advanced deeper into Europe near the end of the war. Historians say up to 200 German warships were scuttled in September 1944 near Prahovo in the Danube gorge as they came under Soviet fire. The idea behind the deliberate sinking was to slow down the Soviet advance in the Balkans. But Nazi Germany surrendered months later, in May 1945. The sight of the old warships is a reminder that the Serbian government, with European Union financial support, has long been trying to do something about them. Some were removed from the river by Communist Yugoslav authorities, but most have remained because of the explosives they carried. Now, however, authorities are trying to keep traffic flowing on the Danube, which flows through 10 nations, as the dropping water levels create dangerous conditions. Experts have linked the unusually hot weather to global warming and other factors. Krsta Brandic, a Prahovo resident, said the low water levels have almost stopped ship traffic: “As you can see, the (big) ships can’t pass anymore."

Suspended Insurance Commission chief vows cooperation, defends vetting standards. Suspended Insurance Commission (IC) Commissioner Reynaldo Regalado said he will cooperate with the proceedings over allegations of favoritism while maintaining that the industry regulator complied with its accreditation standards. “I respect the authority of the Ombudsman and will fully cooperate with the proceedings,” Regalado said in a statement on Wednesday, Aug. 5. “I am confident that the allegations will be fairly and objectively evaluated based on the facts, the evidence, and the applicable law.” Regalado received the preventive suspension order from the Office of the Ombudsman last Tuesday, Aug. 4, following a complaint filed by SCCI Management and Insurance Agency Corp. (SCCI). SCCI’s complaint alleges that the IC chief provided preferential treatment to a third consortium accredited under the passenger personal accident insurance program (PPAIP). PPAIP is a mandatory regulatory framework jointly administered by the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) and the IC. Specifically, SCCI claimed the consortium failed to meet accreditation requirements, submitted documents late, and that the IC did not promptly act on SCCI’s requests for information. Regalado, who filed his counter-affidavits last July 30, maintained that the accreditation process complied with IC Circular Letter (CL) No. 2025-17 and that “all consortiums were evaluated under the same standards.” He further stated that requests for documents were handled in accordance with the law. Supporting this position, the IC noted that Manila Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 180 had previously upheld the validity of CL 2025-17, ruling that the accreditation of a third insurance pool does not violate existing regulations. “Throughout my tenure, I have endeavored to perform my duties with integrity, impartiality, and in the best interest of the public and the Philippine insurance industry,” Regalado said. “I welcome the opportunity to address these allegations through the proper legal process, and remain committed to transparency and accountability.” Information on who will assume Regalado’s role during his suspension remains unavailable. - Derco Rosal

Remulla: No shortcut of legal procedures for Bato once arrested. There will be no shortcut of legal procedures in handling Sen. Ronald “Bato” Dela Rosa once he is nabbed through the arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC), the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said as it denied that the fugitive senator was already collared. DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla said that part of that legal procedure is that Dela Rosa would undergo a booking procedure and will be made to appear in a local court before he would be sent to the Netherlands. Dela Rosa was named as co-perpetrator in the crimes against humanity case over the drug war, the same case that former president Rodrigo Duterte is facing. “We will go to the process as prescribed,” said Remulla, reacting to the reports that Dela Rosa would be sent straight to the Hague once arrested. On Tuesday, social media was inundated by claims and rumors that Dela Rosa was already arrested. Photos of a long-range airplane that was supposed to be spotted in the country also fueled the speculation. But Remulla said Dela Rosa is still at large and is being hunted down. “As of 6 p.m. last night, there has been no arrest for Senator Bato. There has been a lot of speculation that he was arrested and he is being whisked away to the Hague, Rhat’s not true,” said Remulla. He said coordination with the National Bureau of Investigation through the Department of Justice also disputed the claim of arrest. The NBI is under the DOJ while the Philippine National Police is under the DILG. Remulla said he himself was surprised by the rumors but Malacañang said this could be a diversionary tactic from the ongoing impeachment trial. If Dela Rosa is arrested, Remulla vowed that the government will be transparent, “We are always open, We are always transparent in what we do. All the proper channels, all proper procedures will be done according to the rule of law.” Asked of the last monitoring of del Rosa, Remulla said the fugitive senator was last spotted in Mindanao.

Meralco bets on improved smart metering to boost grid resilience. Manuel V. Pangilinan-led power distribution giant Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) is stepping up its grid modernization strategy through continued investments in enhanced smart metering technologies aimed at strengthening its distribution network and reducing electricity losses. In a statement on Wednesday, Aug. 5, Meralco highlighted the evolution of its Elevated Metering Center (EMC) into Elevated Metering Transformation (EMX), a key component of its ongoing drive to deploy smarter and more secure metering infrastructure across its service area. Integrated into Meralco’s broader Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) framework, the upgraded EMX platform allows the utility to perform remote meter reading, service disconnections, and reconnections while providing greater physical protection for its metering facilities. Beyond operational convenience, the company said EMX expands its visibility across the distribution network. This enables the early detection of potential system irregularities and power pilferage while significantly streamlining field operations. For Meralco, strengthening the integrity of its metering system is critical to minimizing non-technical losses—such as illegal connections and meter tampering—while maintaining reliable service for its customers. The EMX rollout forms part of Meralco’s multifaceted grid modernization program. By deploying these smart technologies alongside other digital grid systems, the utility aims to build a more resilient and efficient network capable of meeting the growing energy needs of its more than eight million customers across Metro Manila and nearby provinces. Earlier this year, Meralco said it plans to deploy 72,000 smart meters within the year, in partnership with Aclara Meters Philippines Inc., allowing the distributor to conduct meter readings and process service connections and disconnections remotely. - Gabriell Christel Galang

Japan's Koizumi backs nuclear-free world after controversy. TOKYO, Aug. 5 (Jiji Press) -- Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi has expressed support for a world without nuclear weapons after his proposal for debates without any taboos on nuclear policy sparked controversy, including among hibakusha atomic bombing survivors. "I strongly sympathize with the earnest desire of hibakusha for a world without nuclear weapons," Koizumi told a press conference Tuesday. In an online program last month, Koizumi said that Japan cannot avoid discussions on the difficult issue of nuclear policy. This drew criticism from a hibakusha organization in the western city of Hiroshima, which suffered an atomic bombing on Aug. 6, 1945, in the closing days of World War II. The group said that Koizumi's remark was "unforgivable." "Speaking of defense policy in general, I said that it is important to discuss without excluding any options," Koizumi said Tuesday. "We will continue to work proactively to maintain and strengthen the international system of (nuclear) disarmament and nonproliferation."

Habal-habal driver yields P6.8-M shabu. CEBU CITY – Suspected shabu valued at P6.8 million was seized from a habal-habal driver in Barangay Guadalupe here. The 25-year-old suspect, a certain Ryan, was arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted by the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency-Central Visayas (PDEA-7) and Cebu City Police Office Station 9 at past 2 p.m. on Tuesday, Aug. 3. PDEA-7 Director Joel Plaza said the suspect yielded 40 packs of shabu weighing one kilo. Plaza said the suspect was also arrested in 2023 for illegal drug charges. The suspect was released on probation but the PDEA-7 was informed that he allegedly returned to his illegal drugs activities. The PDEA-7 said that a six-week case buildup showed that the suspect was selling a kilo of shabu a week. Charges for violation of Sections 5 (sale of dangerous drugs) and 11 (possession of dangerous drugs), Article II, of Republic Act No. 9165, the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, will be filed against the suspect, the PDEA 7 said. If found guilty, the suspect may face the maximum penalty of life imprisonment and a fine of up to P10 million.

Philippines optimistic on lifting 12.5% US tariff. The Philippines remains optimistic about the possible removal of the 12.5-percent tariff imposed by the United States (US) on its imports as the Trump administration reviews the country’s efforts to crack down on forced labor imports. Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo said the government is in close coordination with the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) on its ongoing review of the tariffs imposed on Philippine imports. He said the review was prompted by the submission of a joint administrative order (JAO) that outlines an explicit ban on the entry of imported goods suspected or determined to have been produced, wholly or in part, through forced labor. “We are in close coordination with the USTR in terms of their evaluation of the JAO, with the view of having us removed from the tariffs under Section 301,” he told reporters on the sidelines of a forum hosted by the Swiss Chamber of Commerce of the Philippines (SwissCham) last Tuesday, Aug. 4. The USTR imposed a 12.5-percent tariff on the Philippines, alongside 40 other economies, after determining that the country had failed to impose and effectively enforce a prohibition on imports made with forced labor. Under Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974, the USTR is authorized to take action, including imposing tariffs, to eliminate “unfair” foreign practices affecting US commerce, including the importation of goods made with forced labor. While the Philippines has consistently asserted that its trade policies have not been proven to facilitate the entry of imports made with forced labor, the government has nonetheless stepped up its efforts to address the US’ concerns. The JAO, in particular, established an interagency committee tasked with investigating cases involving imports produced through forced labor, which is chaired by the DTI. Through this system, the Bureau of Customs (BOC) will act on the committee’s findings and recommendations to implement measures banning the importation of identified forced labor goods. Earlier, Rodolfo said certain development partners had already expressed their intent to provide funding to support the Philippines in implementing the JAO. Rodolfo said it is still difficult to determine whether the JAO would be sufficient to reduce or remove altogether the 12.5-percent tariff imposed by the US. Still, he noted that the USTR’s response on the matter has been positive so far. Based on the DTI’s preliminary assessment, it is estimated that around 34 percent of the country’s exports to the US are covered by the USTR’s 12.5-percent duty. Exports covered by the tariffs include goods produced by labor-intensive industries, such as leather and travel goods, apparel, footwear, and toys. Last year, exports of these products reached $6.25 billion, DTI data showed. Philippine imports exempt from the tariffs include certain electronic products, agricultural goods, minerals, aircraft parts, and auto parts. Combined, these products reached a total value of $11.98 billion last year. Meanwhile, Rodolfo said the government is still awaiting the findings of the USTR’s probe into structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors, which may result in another set of tariffs. The Philippines is not included in this investigation, but some of its competitors in trade with the US, such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Thailand, are covered. This means the Philippines could soon gain a competitive advantage in shipping products to the US, the country’s largest export market.

COA auditor: OVP, DepEd under Duterte relied on acknowledgement receipts. In the 10 years that he audited over 30 government agencies’ confidential and intelligence fund expenses, Commission on Audit (COA) auditor Roderick Wamil said it was only during Vice President Sara Duterte’s time that he saw a department won’t submit official receipts, relying only on the submission of acknowledge receipts (ARs), during liquidation. At the continuation of the impeachment trial of the Vice President, Wamil told senator-judges that Duterte’s offices—the Office of the Vice President and the Department of Education (DepEd)—only submitted ARs that were not supported by documents substantiating that payment was made. According to Wamil, who was with the COA’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (ICFAO), they needed documents that were supposed to prove to state auditors that the confidential funds requested by the OVP and DepEd for informants reached the intended beneficiaries. “I cannot say it is a standard practice since this is the first time that they submitted purely ARs only to COA,” Wamil said in response to Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan’s question. When Pangilinan pressed if it was his first time to see that only ARs and no sales invoice, no official receipts were submitted, Wamil responded: “Yes, and they submitted a huge number of ARs.” Asked whether the state auditing body can ascertain that the OVP’s confidential funds for the fourth quarter of 2022 and first three quarters of 2023 were indeed used to buy medicines supposedly as payment of rewards to confidential informants, he replied in the negative. “If the official receipt or sales invoice had been submitted to us, we would have been able to tell. However, since only an acknowledgement receipt (AR) was submitted, we cannot determine this based on the document alone,” Wamil said. Wamil was part of the ICFAO from 2014 to 2024. Also, Wamil claimed that the Office of the Vice President refused to comply with the Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM) when confronted about their “unusual” spending. An AOM is a written notice sent by state auditors to a government agency if they find some errors, missing papers, or other irregularities they find during an audit. The meeting took place, but Wamil said COA refused to accede to an audit query, being asked by the camp of the Vice President. “Yes, we did not agree because it’s not in the Joint (Memorandum) Circular, Your Honor,” Wamil said again in response to Pangilinan, confirming they will be violating it if they agreed to an audit query only. But Wamil confirmed the camp of the vice president rejected the AOM the COA issued. “That’s the first time that happened, Your Honor,” Wamil said. “So that’s unusual?” Pangilinan asked. To which Wamil said: “Yes. That’s unusual.” When Sen. Risa Hontiveros asked Wamil if COA was able to confirm if the supposed “Mary Grace Piattos” who received P70,000 worth of medicines as reward was suffering from any illness, he replied in the negative. “I wouldn’t know because there were no documents submitted to us,” he said. When she asked if there is any way the ICFAO can find out what her illness was since the money are considered public funds, Wamil replied that the COA “can make inquiries." “However, since our work is document-based, we can only know what is stated in the documents,” he said. “Yes. We are authorized (to make inquiries) under Section 6.2.3.7 of the Joint Circular,” Wamil further said.

Mark Omega escapes serious injury after scary fall. Titan Ultra breathed a sigh of relief after rookie big man Mark Omega was cleared of any serious injuries following a scary fall during the Giant Risers' 132-128 win over the Macau Giant Pandas on Tuesday, Aug. 4. Giant Risers head coach Rensy Bajar confirmed on Wednesday, Aug. 5, that Omega's CT scan came back negative for any serious injury. The team's medical staff only advised the 25-year-old center to rest for a couple of days. “Okay naman na si Denver. Negative naman yung results niya sa CT scan. Medyo pinapahinga lang siya ng doctor for a couple of days pero okay na siya,” said Bajar. A frightening scene unfolded at the Ninoy Aquino Stadium when Omega landed hard on his back while battling for a rebound just 53 seconds into the fourth quarter. The 6-foot-5 big man laid on the floor for more than five minutes before he was stretchered off the court and rushed to Manila Doctors Hospital. Encouragingly, Omega remained conscious after the incident and was able to move his feet, although he complained of back pain. The injury scare cut short what Bajar believed was shaping up to be Omega's breakout game. Before exiting, the rookie had six points and four rebounds. “Go hard lagi 'yan sa practice. Napakasipag na bata. But pagdating sa game masyado lang siyang nanggigigil. Breakout game na sana kaya lang inabutan nga ng aksidente,” Bajar said after the game.

Cops recover gun flashed by minor in video. CEBU CITY – Police recovered a firearm that a minor in Liloan, northern Cebu brandished through a video he shared in a class group chat. The gun was retrieved after the Liloan Municipal Police Station conducted what it described as a child-sensitive investigation in close coordination with the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office. Police said the principal of Liloan National High School reported to the station's Women and Children Protection Desk that a minor sent a video showing a firearm and other deadly weapons in a group chat. During the interview, the minor voluntarily provided information regarding the firearm seen in the video. Police tracked down the location where the firearm and other deadly weapons were kept. Recovered during the operation were a snub-nose revolver, five live bullets, and brass knuckles with an improvised knife. Police have coordination with the Firearms and Explosives Office to verify the ownership and registration status of the firearm. Further investigation is being conducted to determine the criminal liability of all persons who may have violated Republic Act No. 10591, Presidential Decree No. 9, and other applicable laws, police said. Our immediate priority was to ensure that the firearm was safely recovered and that any threat to the community was addressed. At the same time, we recognize that children who come into conflict with the law deserve interventions that promote accountability, guidance, and rehabilitation, said Police Col. Abubakar Mangelen Jr., chief of the Cebu Provincial Police Office.

GPU will see another jump in prices, may go up as much as 40% amid global memory shortage. Filipino PC builders and gamers are absorbing another round of sticker shock this year, as graphics card prices at local retailers climb well beyond what buyers paid just months ago, and significantly much more than last year. Depending on the model and retailer, increases have ranged from roughly 10% to upwards of 40%, part of a worldwide price shock rippling out from a severe shortage of the memory chips that go into every modern GPU. What's driving the increase The root cause is AI companies buying in massive bulks from manufacturers, creating a strong demand for these products, which then straps the price tag of these memory products to a rocket ship set to fly outside the Solar System's orbit. Video memory chips (GDDR6/GDDR7) used on graphics cards, has been building since late 2025 as manufacturers like Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron redirect production capacity toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI data-center chips. That squeeze has already prompted board partners such as Asus, MSI, and Gigabyte to raise prices on their Nvidia GeForce RTX 50-series and AMD Radeon RX 9000-series cards, with hikes reported in the 10 to 15 percent range depending on VRAM capacity, and AMD reportedly planning to add roughly $10 in cost for every 8GB of video memory on its cards. Local price-tracking sites and builder communities describe a market where prices are shifting faster than shoppers can keep up. Local retailers including PC Express, EasyPC, and DynaQuest PC have been adjusting listed prices to reflect rising acquisition costs from distributors. Some GPUs have already hit as much as 70K PHP. Why it's happening now, and how long it may last Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has publicly said the memory shortage is likely to persist "quite a few years," giving gamers and PC enthusiasts the bad news.

Jonvic eyes human trafficking case vs ex-solon over foiled 'honeytrap' scheme. Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla is eyeing a case of human trafficking against former congressman Jacinto “Jing” Paras over an alleged plot to frame several Cabinet officials and ranking government officials in the so-called “honeytrap” scheme. Human trafficking is a non-bailable offense and Remulla is planning to pursue the case over the use of some women to make affidavits claiming that they were forced to use illegal drugs and have sexual encounters with some Cabinet officials. “It seems that he was the one behind because of his connection with the alleged handler of the women. And it was the handler who disclosed the plan and revealed some names,” said Remulla when asked about the honeytrap scheme. “So Jing Paras is the person of interest, we are investigating him and we are considering filing charges of human trafficking against him,” he stressed. The plan was to get at least five women who would be paid to claim that they were drugged and had sexual encounters with Cabinet officials. The plan was allegedly foiled after the arrest of the supposed handler of the women. The alleged main plan was to frame Executive Secretary Ralph Recto but other personalities are also being targeted like Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon, Remulla and his brother, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla. Batangas Rep Leandro Leviste was tagged as among the brains behind the honeytrap scheme, an allegation that he denied. Asked to comment on the involvement of Leviste, Remulla said it was Paras who mentioned the former’s name to the handler of the women. “I would like to think that Congressman Legarda is a better person but to get to the bottom of it, we need to know the statement of former congressman Jing Paras,” said Remulla.

PAGASA warns heavy rains may persist through weekend. Tropical Storm Maymay (international name “Kujira”) is expected to bring heavy rains over parts of Luzon before the enhanced southwest monsoon or “habagat” keeps wet weather in many areas through the weekend, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Wednesday, Aug. 5. During a press conference, PAGASA weather specialist Benison Estareja said the typhoon internationally named “Dolphin,” which remains outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR), will gradually strengthen the habagat as Maymay weakens after its expected landfall over Northern Luzon. “Unti-unti nitong palalakasin yung southwest monsoon o ‘hanging habagat’ sa malaking bahagi ng ating bansa lalo na po the moment na humina at malusaw itong si Bagyong Maymay sa susunod po na 24 to 48 hours (Typhoon Dolphin will gradually strengthen the southwest monsoon over a large part of the country, especially once Tropical Storm Maymay weakens and dissipates within the next 24 to 48 hours),” Estareja said. ‘Maymay’ nears landfall As of 10 a.m., the center of Tropical Storm Maymay was located 185 kilometers west northwest of Bacnotan, La Union. It had maximum sustained winds of 65 kilometers per hour (kph), gusts of up to 80 kph, and was moving northward at 10 kph. Estareja said Maymay is forecast to generally move eastward over the next 36 hours and may make landfall between La Union and Ilocos Sur on Wednesday evening while still a tropical storm. After interacting with land, Maymay is expected to weaken into a tropical depression as it crosses portions of Ilocos Region and Cordillera Administrative Region. It may further weaken into a low-pressure area over Cagayan Valley by Thursday afternoon, Aug. 6. Meanwhile, Typhoon Dolphin was located 1,765 kilometers east northeast of extreme Northern Luzon as of 10 a.m. It had maximum sustained winds of 155 kph, gusts of up to 190 kph, and was moving west northwestward at 15 kph. Wind signals remain in effect Based on PAGASA’s Tropical Cyclone Bulletin No. 5, Wind Signal No. 2 remained hoisted over Ilocos Sur, northern and central portions of La Union (Luna, Caba, Santol, Bauang, City of San Fernando, San Juan, Bagulin, Aringay, Bangar, San Gabriel, Burgos, Naguilian, Bacnotan, Sudipen, Balaoan), northwestern portion of Pangasinan (Anda, Bolinao, Bani), southwestern portion of Abra (Manabo, Pidigan, Langiden, Luba, Boliney, Sallapadan, Bucloc, Tubo, Villaviciosa, Pilar, Peñarrubia, San Isidro, San Quintin, Bangued, Bucay, Danglas, La Paz, Tayum), western portion of Mountain Province (Besao, Tadian, Bauko, Sagada, Sabangan), and northwestern portion of Benguet (Mankayan, Kapangan, Kibungan, Sablan, Bakun). Signal No. 1 remained in effect over Ilocos Norte, the rest of La Union, the rest of Pangasinan, Apayao, the rest of Abra, Kalinga, the rest of Mountain Province, Ifugao, the rest of Benguet, Cagayan, Isabela, Quirino, Nueva Vizcaya, northern portion of Zambales (Candelaria, Santa Cruz, Masinloc, Palauig), northern portion of Tarlac (Mayantoc, San Clemente, Camiling, Santa Ignacia, Gerona, Paniqui, Moncada, San Manuel, Anao, Ramos, Pura), northern portion of Nueva Ecija (Carranglan, Lupao, Cuyapo, Talugtug, Nampicuan, Guimba, Science City of Muñoz, San Jose City, Pantabangan), and northern and central portions of Aurora (Dilasag, Casiguran, Dinalungan, Dipaculao). Heavy rains, flood risks Estareja said the next 24 hours will be critical as the combined effects of Maymay and the enhanced southwest monsoon are expected to bring widespread rains over most of Luzon. “Within the next 24 hours, crucial part po ito because we're seeing na yung epekto nitong si Bagyong Maymay plus the southwest monsoon mararamdaman po sa malaking bahagi ng Luzon, lalo na sa western section (The next 24 hours are crucial because we expect the combined effects of Tropical Storm Maymay and the southwest monsoon to be felt across much of Luzon, particularly the western section),” he said. From Wednesday to Thursday noon, PAGASA said La Union and Benguet may receive more than 200 millimeters of rainfall, or intense to torrential rains. Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, Abra, and Zambales may receive 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall, or heavy to intense rains. Meanwhile, Ilocos Norte, Apayao, Kalinga, Mountain Province, Ifugao, Nueva Vizcaya, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Bataan, Pampanga, and Bulacan may experience 50 to 100 millimeters of rainfall, or moderate to heavy rains. From Thursday noon to Friday noon, Aug. 7, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, and Benguet may still receive 50 to 100 millimeters of rainfall due to Maymay. The habagat is also expected to bring moderate to heavy rainfall over Metro Manila, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro from Wednesday to Thursday noon. From Thursday noon to Friday noon, Occidental Mindoro may receive 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall, while Zambales, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, and Antique may experience 50 to 100 millimeters. Estareja said rains may persist through the weekend and even into early next week as Typhoon Dolphin continues to enhance the southwest monsoon. “Make sure po na coordinated tayo sa ating mga local government units kung kinakailangan po ng rescue or evacuation. And we're talking of antecedent rainfall, ilang araw na po magkakaroon ng mga pag-ulan. So the moment na mayroon tayong pag-ulan, pagsapit po ng weekend, mas tumataas ang banta ng mga flash floods at landslides (Make sure we are coordinated with our local government units if rescue or evacuation becomes necessary. We are talking about antecedent rainfall, with several days of rain expected. By the weekend, the threat of flash floods and landslides will become even higher),” he said.

'Walang consumption': House leaders seek VAT removal from system loss charges. Top leaders from the House of Representatives have filed a measure seeking to exempt electricity consumers from paying the 12 percent Value-Added Tax (VAT) on the much-panned system loss charges. Filed by Senior Deputy Speaker South Cotabato Cotabato 2nd district Rep. Ferdinand Hernandez and Committee on Ways and Means Chairman Marikina City 2nd district Rep. Miro Quimbo, the measure, House Bill (HB) No. 10602, was described Wednesday, Aug. 5 as a fiscally responsible and consumer-oriented complement to ongoing efforts in the House to lower electricity costs. These were seen as offshoots of President Marcos' pronouncements during his July 27 State of the Nation Address (SONA) before a joint session of Congress. According to Quimbo, the VAT exemption in HB No. 10602 will apply only to the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC)-approved recoverable distribution system loss charges reflected in electricity bills. Quimbo explained that the bill advances the objective of reducing electricity costs for Filipinos while also recognizing the realities faced by the country’s power distribution sector. “Everyone agrees that consumers deserve lower electricity bills. The question is how we provide that relief without unintentionally weakening smaller electric utilities and cooperatives that keep the lights on, particularly in far-flung communities,” said the economist-solon. The proposal comes as discussions continue on HB No. 10430, earlier filed by Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III and Majority Leader Sandro Marcos, which seeks to remove recoverable system loss charges under the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) —a direct response to President Marcos’ call in his SONA that consumers should not shoulder the burden of system loss. 'Clear inequity' “Removing the VAT on system loss charges is a straightforward way of lowering electricity bills today," Quimbo said. "As Congress continues to fine-tune longer-term reforms, we can already correct one clear inequity: consumers should not be taxed on electricity they never actually consumed,” he said, referring to the concept of system loss. According to the veteran lawmaker, VAT is a tax imposed whenever value is added to consumption. Since it is not consumed by the consumer, no value is added, and therefore VAT should not imposed, Quimbo explained. “Our proposal addresses the tax treatment of system loss. Whether broader reforms to the system loss mechanism are eventually adopted is a separate policy discussion. What is clear is that if there is no actual consumption, there should be no VAT,” he added. Quimbo emphasized that his measure forms part of broader efforts in Congress to provide targeted tax relief to Filipino families without compromising the fiscal sustainability of government or the operational viability of the country's power sector. “Every peso saved on an electricity bill matters. This proposal provides meaningful relief to consumers while ensuring that reforms remain practical, balanced, and sustainable,” he said.

Maymay, 'habagat' disrupt classes, affect 1,700 families in Pangasinan, La Union. MALASIQUI, Pangasinan – Tropical storm Maymay (international name Kujira) and the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) have affected 1,775 families and led to the suspension of classes in La Union and Pangasinan. The La Union Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO), in its situation report as of 5 a.m. on Wednesday, said the weather disturbances affected 1,735 families or 4,989 individuals in 51 barangays of La Union. It added that 213 families or 653 individuals are staying inside eight evacuation centers while 338 families or 757 individuals are staying outside evacuation centers. Affected families are from Bacnotan, Bangar, Agoo, Aringay, Bagulin, Bauang, Burgos, Caba, Naguilian, and Santo Tomas. PDRRMO recorded 31 incidents of flooding along with five incidents of landslide, rockslide, and mudslide, and one incident of a fallen tree. Thirty-four barangays are still experiencing power interruptions in Bauang and Naguilian and San Fernando City. Seven houses were partially damaged in Bauang. The provincial government of La Union, in a statement, said the local executives of the affected towns and city are monitoring the situation on the ground. "They have provided initial aid to the affected families and are focused on clearing operations on the roads and landslide-affected areas," it stated. Classes on all levels, in public and private schools and work in government offices, except those on the frontline, are suspended. Meanwhile, a localized suspension of classes was also implemented in 47 out of the 48 local government units in Pangasinan amid the threat of heavy rainfall. The provincial government said LGUs decide based on their monitoring of the situation in their areas, while in Binalonan, it was left to the discretion of schools. "We are expecting, based on the heavy rainfall outlook, 100 to 200 millimeters of moderate to intense accumulated rainfall within 24 hours and 50 to 100 millimeters on Thursday," said Pangasinan PDRRMO emergency head Pia Flores in a phone interview. Flores said a total of 40 families or 125 individuals in Alaminos City and Bani are in evacuation centers as of Wednesday. While flooding subsided in some localities, some barangays in Lingayen and Calasiao are reportedly flooded. A minor landslide was also reported in Bolinao. "There are no reported injured or damaged houses so far," she said. She added that authorities are also monitoring river systems as runoff from the mountains is expected to swell waterways in the coming days and may trigger flooding in low-lying areas. As of 5 a.m., tropical cyclone wind signal no. 2 is up in the northern and central parts of La Union and in Anda, Bolinao, and Bani in Pangasinan, while the rest of La Union and Pangasinan are under signal no. 1 due to Maymay. La Union Gov. Mario Eduardo Ortega assured residents that the provincial government is fully prepared to respond to flooding, landslides, and tropical cyclones, stressing that disaster readiness has long been a priority for the province. Ortega noted that La Union is frequently affected by tropical cyclones, similar to neighboring regions such as Region 2, the Cordillera Administrative Region, and Catanduanes. Due to exposure to severe weather, the province maintains a proactive approach to disaster preparedness whenever storms threaten, he said. Ortega said the provincial government of La Union (PGLU), together with all local government units, immediately mobilizes resources and personnel whenever adverse weather conditions are expected. He said that as early as two months ago, the provincial government has prepositioned relief supplies for residents who may need to evacuate. These resources are complemented by assistance from national government agencies, including the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), the Office of Civil Defense (OCD), and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH). Ortega added that disaster response efforts are being carried out through close coordination with the Armed Forces of the Philippines, including the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Philippine Coast Guard, as well as the Philippine National Police, ensuring a unified response to any emergency.

Eala faces Parks, reunites with Venus in busy Toronto opener. Alex Eala hopes to keep her momentum rolling on the WTA Tour as she opens her National Bank Open campaign against familiar foe Alycia Parks in Toronto, Canada, on Thursday, Aug. 6 (Philippine time). Fresh off her breakthrough title at the Mubadala DC Open in Washington, D.C. last Monday, Aug. 4, the Filipina tennis sensation is seeking to carry her hot form and to turn the tables on the American in their opening-round clash set no earlier than 8:10 a.m. (PH time). It would be a busy day for Eala as she is also expected to return not earlier than 10 p.m. with tennis icon Venus Williams as they reunite in the doubles and clash with Liudmila Samsonova and Miyu Kato in the first round. Eala’s first and only meeting against Parks was at the 2026 Australian Open last January, where the Filipina lost, 0-6, 6-3, 6-2. But much has changed since then, with both players having made significant strides in the rankings. Eala surged from No. 49 at the time to career-high No. 20 this week, while Parks has also improved, climbing from No. 99 to No. 71. More than extending her impressive run on Tour and redeeming herself against Parks, Eala is more excited to play before an expected big crowd. “I’ve been told that it’s going to be a full house (tomorrow). So, I’m really very excited to see and experience the atmosphere,” Eala said in a press briefing. “It’s nice to see that the Filipino community is really showing up and they’re enjoying tennis and hopefully, it will help grow the sport as well. And in the end, give them something, a new experience and a joyful experience,” she added. Eala is also expected to be cautious of what lies ahead deeper in the bracket, where she is in the lower half of the draw that has reigning Wimbledon champion and sixth seed Linda Noskova, No. 21 Marie Bouzkova, No. 12 Belinda Bencic, qualifier Sloane Stephens, and good friend No. 13 Iva Jovic, to name a few.

Noceja, Condez cruise to Round of 16.
