'Kanina ka pa!': Imee, COA auditor clash over VP Sara confidential fund accountability. Senator-Judge Imee Marcos on Tuesday quizzed Commission on Audit (COA) auditor Roderick Wamil over his interpretation of the COA-Department of Budget and Management Joint Circular on accountability for confidential funds, while also questioning his earlier testimony that Vice President Sara Duterte was the only vice president audited for confidential funds. During her interpellation, Marcos focused on the Joint Circular's provision on the "accountable officer," arguing that the presumption of misappropriation for failure to liquidate public funds should apply to the designated Special Disbursing Officer (SDO), who has custody of the funds, rather than the Vice President. Marcos cited the circular's definition of an accountable officer and asserted that in the Office of the Vice President, the designated SDO—not the Vice President—was the payee and custodian of the confidential funds. Wamil, however, disagreed with her interpretation. He said the Joint Circular also assigns responsibilities to the head of the agency, including approving cash advances, overseeing the utilization of confidential funds, and ensuring compliance with the circular's provisions. He maintained that the term "accountable officer" is not limited to the SDO alone. The exchange became tense after Marcos accused Wamil of giving inconsistent answers and urged him to respond with a simple "yes" or "no," while Wamil said he could not categorically answer because other provisions of the Joint Circular also applied. "Ang liwanag sa definition ng Joint Circular. Mag-yes or no ka lang. Kanina ka pa. Inaaway mo ko lagi (It's very clear in the definition of the Joint Circular. Just answer yes or no. I've been asking you for a while now. You've been arguing with me the whole time)," Marcos said. Presiding Officer Senator-judge Francis "Chiz" Escudero, presiding over the trial, reminded Wamil to avoid arguing with the senator-judges. Marcos also revisited Wamil's testimony from the previous day that Vice President Duterte was the first and only vice president whose confidential funds had been audited by COA. She pointed to a 2014 Special Allotment Release Order (SARO), presented earlier by the defense, showing that then-Vice President Jejomar Binay had been allocated P6-million in confidential funds. Marcos asked how that could be reconciled with Wamil's earlier statement. Wamil responded that while the SARO showed an allotment, COA's Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (ICFAO) only audits confidential funds after liquidation reports are submitted. He said that based on COA's records, only Duterte's office submitted liquidation reports for confidential funds, which was why she was the only vice president audited by the office. Wamil added that COA could not determine whether Binay's confidential funds had been used because no liquidation report had been submitted. Marcos questioned why COA would not know whether Binay had received confidential funds despite the existence of the SARO, ending the exchange by remarking that COA appeared to have many instances where it "didn't know."

Trump says deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz could come as early as Wednesday. CAIRO (AP) — U.S. President Donald Trump said a deal on the Strait of Hormuz could come as early as Wednesday or Thursday, while Iran and Oman inched toward an agreement to reopen the critical waterway and potentially help bring an end to the war. Trump was asked by reporters traveling with him in California about a report on the Axios news site that an announcement on the Strait of Hormuz could be made on Wednesday. “It could happen. Tomorrow or the next day,” he said, speaking on Tuesday evening California time, which was already Wednesday morning in the Middle East. “A lot of progress has been made.” Oil prices eased on hopes of progress for a deal that would allow oil tankers to freely exit the Persian Gulf again and deliver crude around the world. Brent crude, the international standard, slipped by 1.2% to $78.43 per barrel early Wednesday. The agreement would see routes controlled by Iran and Oman, regional officials tell AP The possible agreement emerging from talks between Iran and Oman calls for ships to enter the Persian Gulf through an Iranian-controlled route and exit through a route controlled by Oman, two regional officials told The Associated Press. Service fees would be charged for providing security and preserving the maritime environment, the officials said. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the sensitive negotiations. The Trump administration has previously ruled out any deal that would give Iran control over the strait, which was an open international waterway before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28. About one fifth of the world’s oil and natural gas passed through the strait, but shipping through the waterway has been reduced to a trickle at best by Iran’s attacks since the start of the war. In an exchange with reporters on Monday, the U.S. president reiterated his public opposition to tolls being charged in the strait. “I’m not going to let them charge,” Trump said. “Anybody’s going to charge, we’ll charge.” The regional officials said negotiations are still underway and that the final agreement could take a different form, with any deal linked to lifting the U.S. blockade on Iran’s ports. US and Iranian officials say progress is being made Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said Tuesday that Tehran’s talks with Oman were focused on “establishing safe inbound and outbound shipping lanes,” routes that “uphold sovereign rights while also addressing the national security considerations of both Iran and Oman.” “The final results of these negotiations will be announced once concluded,” he added, according to Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed progress had been made in those talks, “but not finality yet.” Rubio has previously ruled out any deal that would give Iran control over the strait, saying last month that would create a “very dangerous precedent” for other parts of the world. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that “there is a chance we may have a deal today or tomorrow to open the strait and move towards a more normalized position in this conflict.” Arab countries seek to broker an end to the war Qatar’s emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, said he also spoke to Trump by phone on Tuesday as the Arab country tries to broker a resolution to the war. Al Thani’s office said the two discussed ways to bridge the divide “in a way that enhances the prospects of reaching a sustainable diplomatic settlement to the crisis.” Trump is under mounting pressure to end an unpopular war that has driven up gas prices ahead of midterm elections and drawn down U.S. supplies of some munitions. In recent days, he has again alternately threatened massive strikes and voiced support for diplomatic efforts. Trump said Monday that the U.S. was in talks with Iran, saying it was Tehran’s “last chance” to reach a deal and avoid another U.S. military escalation. “The first phase is the opening of the straits. The second phase will be the denuclearization,” Trump said. “And that will take a little while.” Iran has denied it is negotiating with the U.S., saying the talks are only with Oman. Ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz and in Red Sea An Indian-flagged commercial ship sank Tuesday in the Red Sea off Yemen after being struck by an explosive-laden boat, Yemeni and Indian authorities said. Yemen’s coast guard rescued the crew, which included 13 Indians and a Yemeni. There was no immediate claim of responsibility, but Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants have repeatedly struck ships traversing the Red Sea near Yemen. Last month, the Houthis announced they were closing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait that leads to the Red Sea for Saudi-linked shipping in retaliation for the kingdom’s blockade on Yemen and an attack on the international airport in Yemen’s rebel-held capital, Sanaa. Earlier Tuesday, a cargo ship reported being “hit by an unknown projectile” while traversing the Strait of Hormuz, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center. The center said the reported strike damaged the vessel at around 2 a.m. local time while it was about 37 kilometers (23 miles) northeast of Al Khasab, a port city in Oman. The British maritime security firm Ambrey said the ship sustained damage.

AboitizPower partners with South Korea’s KHNP to explore nuclear power shift. Aboitiz Power Corp. signed a preliminary agreement with South Korea’s state-run nuclear operator as the Philippine power generator evaluates commercial atomic energy to reinforce national energy security and accelerate its transition to low-carbon electricity generation. Under the non-binding memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed at the headquarters of Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power Co. (KHNP) in Gyeongju, South Korea, both companies agreed to pursue joint pre-feasibility studies, cross-border technical information sharing, and specialized capacity-building activities. The framework will focus on assessing emerging and commercial nuclear power technologies to determine how atomic generation can fit into the long-term Philippine energy matrix. The partnership comes as domestic power producers face growing pressure to secure stable and low-carbon baseload electricity while expanding renewable energy portfolios. AboitizPower, one of the country’s largest power producers with assets spanning thermal, hydro, solar, and geothermal power, said the arrangement is a structured mechanism to test the technical and economic viability of nuclear assets. “This MOU marks a meaningful step in AboitizPower’s efforts to understand nuclear energy’s potential contribution to the Philippines’ energy security,” said Carlos Ramon Aboitiz, the company’s chief corporate services officer. He noted that any potential commercial deployment of nuclear capacity must be grounded in strict technical assessments and robust regulatory frameworks. The Department of Energy (DOE) has increasingly advocated for international knowledge transfers and public-private coordination to ensure power grid resilience. Energy Secretary Sharon Garin explained that cross-border technical partnerships are pivotal to achieving the nation’s energy transition goals. “The transition toward a secure, clean, and reliable energy future cannot be achieved by government alone,” Garin said. “It requires strong public-private coordination and the exchange of best practices across borders with experienced industry leaders such as KHNP,” she added. South Korea’s KHNP accounts for roughly 32.76 percent of its home country’s total electricity output and operates 26 nuclear units. The Korean company brings significant international experience to the partnership, having constructed the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the United Arab Emirates and currently advancing new nuclear projects in the Czech Republic. Il-kyung Choi, KHNP’s senior executive vice president for business development and management, emphasized that the firm intends to leverage its construction and operational expertise—both domestically and internationally—to support the Philippines’ clean energy objectives. For AboitizPower, exploring nuclear capability aligns with broader corporate efforts to diversify power generation and address grid supply constraints without compromising climate targets. While the agreement remains exploratory, it underscores the expanding involvement of private energy companies in evaluating advanced nuclear generation for the Southeast Asian nation. (Gabriiell Christel Galang)

Top juniors, rising stars set for Olivarez netfest showdown. The country’s top junior tennis talents, rising stars and promising newcomers converge beginning Thursday, Aug. 6, for what is expected to be a fierce battle for titles and valuable ranking points in the Mayor Edwin Olivarez Juniors Age Group Tennis Championships in Sucat, Parañaque. A total of 256 players will compete across eight boys’ and girls’ age-group divisions, each featuring a full 32-player draw – a rare turnout that highlights the sustained growth of junior tennis and the surge in interest generated by Alex Eala’s breakthrough success on the international stage. Leading the girls’ premier 18-and-under division are Ayl Gonzaga, Ava Banson, Jana Bermejo and Jasmine Sardona, who hope to emulate Eala’s rise. Also in the hunt are Melatiah Pascua, Agatha Asistio, Sofia Demadara and Cristina Reyes. Gonzaga, Banson, Sardona and Bermejo likewise headline the 16-and-U category, where they will be challenged by Francine Wong, fresh from a twin-title sweep in last week’s Palawan Junior Series stop in San Pablo City, Laguna. The tournament serves as the second leg of the Luzon swing of the Palawan Junior Series, which was launched nationwide earlier this year by Palawan Pawnshop president and CEO Bobby Castro following successful three-leg circuits in Mindanao and the Visayas. It also forms part of the Olivarez family’s continuing commitment to grassroots tennis development by providing young players with a high-level competitive platform. With the record turnout, organizers will utilize both the Olivarez Sports Center and the Parañaque indoor courts, with matches to be played on clay throughout the tournament. Nicholas Andala, Martin Paulsen, Anthony Cosca and Nathan Cansana spearhead the boys’ 18-and-U field, but they are expected to face stiff resistance from Vivaan Garg, Jairo Flores, Akio Kue and Bien Tulop in the Group 2 event sanctioned by Philta and Universal Tennis Ranking and presented by Dunlop. Andala, Cosca, Garg, Kue and Flores also bolster the 16-and-U division alongside Antonio Bengzon, Jan Villeno and Tyronne Caro. Villeno and Caro, meanwhile, emerge as the top seeds in the 14-and-U class, which also features Yuan Torrente, Jfsky Berille, Juan Antonio Cablitas, Djokovic Garcia, Don Simplicio Bermejo and Liam Harrow. Fresh from upsetting top seed Harrow to capture the 12-and-U title in San Pablo, Lance Recto seeks another championship but must again contend with Harrow, as well as Raven Licayan, Rafael Cablitas and Leonardo Manio III in another loaded field. In the girls’ 14-and-U division, Leanne Barrido and Wong head the favorites, although Jaynelle Castro, Talitha Lopez, Riomy Ambrad, Megumi Deura, Julia Bermejo and Arabela Barandiaran have the talent to mount serious title bids. Eilythia Comia also shoots for back-to-back girls’ 12-and-U crowns after her San Pablo triumph, with Castro, Misty May Principe, Margaret Abacan, Brielle Loyola, Abrielle Asistio, Caitleen Villacortes and Blaire Rada all eager to deny her repeat bid in the tournament backed by ICON Golf & Sports and the Palawan Group of Companies. The Luzon swing concludes on Aug. 20-30 with the Gentry Juniors at the Colegio de San Agustin Tennis Stadium in San Jose del Monte, Bulacan, before culminating with the Gentry Open. For details and registration, interested participants may contact tournament director Bobby Mangunay at 0915-404-6464.

Classes, work in Southern Mindanao cancelled due to magnitude-6.4 quake. DAVAO CITY – Provinces suspended classes and work in government offices following a magnitude-6.4 earthquake that rocked Southern Mindanao on Wednesday, Aug. 5. The provincial government of Sarangani and city government of General Santos cancelled face-to-face classes on all levels and work in government offices. However, the directive does not cover agencies involved in disaster response and other essential services. Sultan Kudarat Gov. Datu Pax Ali Mangudadatu suspended afternoon classes on all levels in public and private schools. “Students, parents, teachers, and school personnel are advised to remain vigilant, observe safety protocols, and continue monitoring official advisories from concerned authorities,” Mangudadatu said. Classes on all levels were also suspended in the city of Kidapawan in Cotabato. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology said the earthquake’s epicenter was 29 kilometers south of Balut Island in Davao Occidental with a depth of 13 kilometers. It was felt at Intensity 5 in Glan, Sarangani and Intensity 4 in Kiamba, Alabel, and Malungon, also in Sarangani; General Santos City, and Tupi and Polomolok in South Cotabato. The earthquake struck as many of these areas are still reeling from the impact of the magnitude-7.8 earthquake last June 8 that left a trail of death and destruction in the provinces of Davao Occidental and Sarangani.

San Juan rebounds, routs Negros. The San Juan Knights hit high gear in the second half and proceeded to rout the Negros Hacienderos, 120-96, on Tuesday, Aug. 4, and rebound in the SportsPlus MPBL (Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League) at the Ynares Center Montalban in Rizal Province. Held to a 54-48 lead, the Knights poured in 33 points each in the third and fourth quarters to secure their 15th win against two losses, the last against the Quezon Huskers (71-78) on July 30, in the round-robin elimination phase of the two-division, 26-team tournament. AC Soberano shone for San Juan with 22 points, spiked by six triples. 3 rebounds and 2 assists, and was chosen the SportsPlus best player over Mike Calisaan with 17 points, 2 rebounds and 3 assists. "That loss (against Quezon) was painful for us," said Soberano. "We made adjustments, and it worked." Veteran Rey Hugnatan supported with 12 points and 5 rebounds, and so did Patrick Sleat with 10 points, including the Knights' last eight, 3 rebounds and 3 assists. Soberano said they (Knights) need to step up following the departure of key players Michael Phillips bound for the Japan B. League, and Gerry Abadiano, bound for the Korean Basketball League. Powered by Flever Dignadice and DJ Howe, Negros led, 25-22, before San Juan took control at the half, 54-48, behind the efforts of Soberano and Calisaan. Negros tumbled to 1-17, the worst in the South division, despite DJ Howe's 22 points, 5 assists and 3 rebounds, and Michael Alvarez's 16 points, 10 rebounds and 5 assists. Dignadice finished with 11 points and Lorenz Vajar 11. The tournament returns to the FilOil EcoOil Centre in San Juan on Thursday, featuring games between Bulacan and Pasig at 3 p.m., Bataan and Abra at 5 p.m., and Paranaque and Basilan at 7 p.m.

DepEd to distribute metal detectors to all schools. The Department of Education will provide metal detectors to all public schools across the country as part of the safety measures amid concerns on students carrying deadly weapons. DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara said they plan to buy metal detectors and distribute them to prevent and discourage students from carrying and sneaking bladed weapons and other deadly weapons into their schools. “Based on our audit, a number of schools need metal detectors which are important because there are students who are carrying knives and other items,” said Angara in an interview during the Ceremonial Signing of Implementing Rules and Regulations for the Early Childhood Care and Development or ECCD System Act. For Angara, the purchase of metal detectors are logical since it does not entail huge budgets like hiring of more security guards to secure every school in the country. Angara earlier disclosed that they are planning to hire security guards but cited budgetary constraints. “We are already procuring them (metal detectors) because it only costs thousands of pesos. And we will provide all schools with that,” said Angara. The school security measures cropped up over several incidents of violence in schools, including the first school mass shooting in Tacloban and the recent was the knife attack in a school in Las Piñas City. Aside from metal detectors and hiring of security guards, Angara said they already sought assistance from the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) in tapping policemen and barangay security officers for school security. He said the presence of policemen and barangay tanod outside the schools is of big help in maintaining peace and order, as well as the safety of both the learners and school personnel.

3 Filipino niche perfume brands every fragrance lover should know. The global fragrance boom has sparked a new generation of perfume enthusiasts, and the Philippines is no exception. But while international perfume houses continue to dominate wish lists, more Filipino fragrance lovers are turning their attention to homegrown niche brands. Created by passionate perfumers and inspired by deeply personal stories, these local labels are proving that Filipino-made fragrances can stand alongside their global counterparts. From scents inspired by resilience and romance to bottles that preserve culture and memories, these three rising brands deserve a spot on every fragrance lover's radar. Valor Extrait de Parfum The road to success is rarely smooth. It is often filled with sacrifices, sleepless nights, setbacks, and lessons. For founder John David San Andres, these experiences inspired behind Valor Extrait de Parfum. "This scent exists because of every challenge, every lesson, and every person who became part of the journey," he said. "This is more than a fragrance. This is a reminder that no matter how many times life breaks you, you can still become the man you were destined to be." The brand now carries seven fragrances and has also earned a place on Fragrantica, one of the world's largest online fragrance platforms, where several of its creations have received positive reviews from perfume enthusiasts. If you're new to the brand, start with All Eyes on You, a fresh yet comforting scent that evokes the feeling of slipping into a crisp white shirt before being wrapped in a warm embrace. Woody accords and creamy vanilla make it both familiar and sophisticated. Those who enjoy gourmand fragrances should try Secret Indulgence, one of the sexiest locally made gourmand scents currently available, balancing sweetness with elegance instead of becoming overly sugary. Dilettante Perfumery Named after the Italian verb dilettare, meaning “to delight,” Dilettante Perfumery is the newest venture of young perfumer Paolo Pascua. Officially launching on Aug. 8, the brand introduces thoughtfully crafted compositions that bring something fresh to the local niche fragrance scene. "I called my brand Dilettante to serve as a reminder to myself that there's nothing wrong with being a beginner," he said. "It might seem intimidating at first, but Dilettante is all about embracing the art and hard work of creation. We are all dilettantes in one way or another. Dilettante invites everyone to relish it." Among its upcoming releases, Temple of Dawn, Forever, and Creature Feature stand out. Temple of Dawn is made for coffee lovers. Instead of smelling like a freshly brewed cup, it delivers the soft, lingering warmth of coffee in a refined skin scent. Forever captures the feeling of walking hand in hand with someone you love by the sea. Honey and vanilla create a comforting sweetness, while orange, amber, and wisps of smoke add depth and nostalgia. For something darker, Creature Feature leans into mystery. Smoky tobacco, rosemary, and violet leaf create a fragrance that feels like standing outside an old provincial home at night, surrounded by towering trees and an imagination running wild. Imahenacion Founded by Mindanao-based photographer Noel Nacion, Imahenacion transforms photographs, memories, and emotions into wearable scents. His years spent documenting people and life's fleeting moments became the foundation of his perfume creations. One of the brand's most distinctive features is its use of Visayan names, allowing each fragrance to celebrate local language while telling stories that resonate beyond Mindanao. Lakra sa Ulan (Mark on the Pillow) evokes the lingering memory of intimacy, while Akong Pahuway (My Rest) explores the idea that rest is not always a place or simply sleep. Sometimes, it is a person. "Through my lens, I've witnessed so many raw human moments—happiness, quiet sadness, laughter, and tears. Eventually, that passion led me to perfumery. I've always believed that scent has this incredible power to instantly pull us back to a specific moment in time," Noel tells Manila Bulletin Lifestyle. "When I started Imahenacion, it wasn't about trying to be trendy or overly unique—it was simply an outlet for my creativity to bottle memories and emotions that most of us can relate to. For me, it's about turning a feeling you can see into a scent you can wear. It's not all about being a Mindanaoan but about life and memories that we can relate to." Those who want to experience Imahenacion in person can visit the brand during FragCon at Greenhills Mall on Aug. 22 to 23. Together, these brands represent a new chapter for Philippine perfumery. Rather than simply recreating familiar scent profiles, they bottle stories, emotions, and lived experiences, proving that Filipino niche fragrances have found their own voice and are ready to be discovered by the world.

Centeno, Amit storm into world 10-ball quarters. Defending champion Chezka Centeno and Rubilen Amit toppled their respective rivals to advance to the quarterfinals of the 2026 WPA Women’s 10-Ball World Championship in Rome, Italy on Tuesday, Aug. 4 (Wednesday). Centeno turned back American Savannah Easton, 4-1, 2-4, 4-0, 4-1, while Amit outplayed Japanese Yuki Hiraguchi, 4-3, 0-4, 4-2, 4-0, to bolster their respective title bids. The triumph arranged Centeno a duel with Chihiro Kawahara, who swept fellow Japanese Samia Konishi, 4-1, 4-1, 4-0, while Amit next faces Korean Seo Seoa, who edged American Sofia Mast, 4-0, 3-4, 4-0, 4-0. Should Centeno and Amit both prevail in their next assignments, they will arrange a semifinal showdown which is a rematch of last year’s finals.

More than 41,000 residents affected by ‘Luis,’ ‘Maymay,’ ‘habagat’. The combined impact of tropical cyclones “Luis” and “Maymay,” as well as the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) have affected more than 41,000 individuals while around 5,800 persons were displaced as heavy rains continued to disrupt communities in six regions, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) reported on Wednesday, Aug. 5. A report from the OCD said a total of 12,432 families or 41,979 individuals felt the impact of the three weather disturbances in Ilocos (Region 1), Cagayan Valley (Region 2), Central Luzon (Region 3), Bicol (Region 5), Zamboanga Peninsula (Region 9), and the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR). Of the number, a total of 1,821 families or 5,818 persons were staying in 14 evacuation centers The OCD has yet to report any deaths, injuries or missing persons linked to the weather disturbances. It also has not recorded any damage to government infrastructure while one house was reported partially damaged. The government has so far extended P1,221,039 worth of assistance to the affected families. Habagat continued to bring intermittent rains over large parts of Luzon and some areas in the Visayas, prompting evacuations in flood-prone communities. Earlier, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) placed its regional disaster response offices on heightened alert to ensure that relief goods, rescue assets and emergency responders could be mobilized immediately in affected areas. “Our priority is to ensure that all affected families receive the assistance they need while keeping communities safe from further risks posed by continuous rains,” the OCD said. The agency added that “regional offices remain in close coordination with local government units to monitor the situation, support evacuation efforts, and facilitate the immediate delivery of humanitarian assistance.”

Lacson: COA audit rules on confidential, intel funds should be updated, expanded. The Commission on Audit (COA)'s rules governing the audit of confidential and intelligence funds (CIF) should be updated and expanded to ensure greater accountability, Senator-Judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said Wednesday, Aug. 5. In Day 13 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, Lacson raised the need to revisit the Joint Memorandum Circular after COA auditor Roderick Wamil said that the agency's audit of CIF is limited to a document-based compliance audit under current guidelines. The former national police chief also raised the issue of whether auditors assigned to CIFs should be granted appropriate security clearance to access classified documents needed for a thorough audit. Lacson said that aside from relying on documents, physical audits should also be done by COA. “Why are you limited to paper audits? Don't you have physical audits? It seems your current auditing system is lacking. How would you know if the one signing the acknowledgment receipts is a legitimate person if you cannot determine if the person behind the alias is a real person?” Lacson told the COA auditor during his interjection at the Vice President's impeachment trial. The senator cited his experience in intelligence operations during his law enforcement career and when he was the Philippine National Police (PNP) chief. “You may want to recommend an amendment to your Joint Memorandum Circular. Your current auditing process is lacking. In fairness to the concerned offices or persons being audited, due process must be complete,” he pointed out. “If you rely on documents only based on your joint memorandum circular, you don't go beyond that,” he added. Wamil, who served with the COA's Intelligence and Confidential Fund Audit Office (ICFAO) from September 2014 to February 2024, said that the ICFAO's compliance audit is conducted in accordance with the provisions of the Joint Memorandum Circular. During his stint with the ICFAO, Wamil audited the liquidation reports for the confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education (DepEd). Lacson raised the issue on the auditing rules on CIFs after Wamil testified that the Joint Memorandum Circular does not prescribe a specific document to establish the success of a surveillance or intelligence operation. He suggested that after-surveillance or after-intelligence reports be recognized as evidence of the success of a surveillance or intelligence-gathering activity. Wamil admitted that auditors currently determine compliance by looking for a "causal link" between the information provided by an informer and the outcome of the operation. “Would an after-surveillance or after-intelligence report of a particular agent suffice to be considered as evidence of success? I'm not referring to the entire operation. But if you conduct surveillance and prepare an after-surveillance report, would you consider that as an evidence of success?" he said. At the same time, Lacson also questioned how auditors can conduct a thorough audit of CIFs without the appropriate security clearance to access classified documents. He explained that classified documents, including the true identities corresponding to the aliases used in intelligence operations, remain secured until the intelligence-gathering project is terminated and the documents are declassified. Lacson said that without the appropriate security clearance, auditors cannot be expected to fully examine the nature of an intelligence project or operation. “How can you audit properly if you do not know the nature of the intelligence project or operation?” he pointed out. Prior to Lacson's interjection, Wamil defended COA's move to audit CIFs, stating that "confidential funds are still public funds." Wamil pointed this out when Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel "Migz" Zubiri questioned him about the notion that confidential funds are exempt from the agency's strict audit scrutiny. "Obviously Mr. Witness, when you say 'confidential in nature,' it's like saying 'don't ask anymore, as long as we used the money.' In your view, is that correct or not?" Zubiri said in questioning Wamil. Wamil replied that such notion is incorrect: "Confidential funds are still public funds and therefore, should be subject to strict accounting and auditing rules."

QC guard foils helmet theft, suspect nabbed. A 27-year-old man was nabbed after a security guard foiled his attempt to steal a P4,000 motorcycle helmet from a parked motorcycle inside an establishment along Commonwealth Avenue, Barangay Holy Spirit, Quezon City, on Monday night, Aug. 3. The suspect, identified only as alias “Mar,” entered the establishment through the parking exit riding a gray Honda Click motorcycle while wearing an Angkas blue long-sleeve uniform. The on-duty security guard noticed the suspect's suspicious behavior and kept him under observation inside the parking area. Moments later, the guard saw the suspect take a white EVO full-face helmet from another parked motorcycle and place it inside the top box of his motorcycle before attempting to leave the premises. The guard immediately stopped the suspect from escaping and coordinated with the AFNI Call Center to locate the helmet owner, who later identified the recovered helmet as his. Quezon City Police District Director Randy Glenn Silvio said the suspect is facing a theft complaint, with the case being prepared for inquest before the Quezon City Prosecutor's Office. Police records also showed that the suspect had previous cases involving illegal gambling and violation of the New Anti-Carnapping Act of 2016.

Village chair, 2 pals nabbed in drug sting. TACLOBAN CITY – A barangay chairman and two companions were arrested in a buy-bust operation on Bypass Road, Barangay San Jose, Palo, Leyte, on Tuesday. Police identified the suspects as barangay chairman Mario, 35, Rank 1 Regional Priority Target Listed (RPTL) High-Value Individual (HVI); and Jessa, 34, and Josh, 18, all are residents of Leyte, Leyte. Recovered from them were seven heat-sealed transparent plastic sachets containing suspected shabu weighing 805 grams and a Dangerous Drugs Board (DDB) value of P5,474,000. Police Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy, PRO-8 director, lauded operating units for the successful operation. "The arrest of the region's Rank 1 HVI is a major accomplishment in our anti-illegal drug campaign. We will continue conducting intelligence-driven operations and strengthening partnerships to keep Eastern Visayas safe and drug-free," he said. He encouraged the public to stay vigilant and support law enforcement by reporting illegal drug activities in their communities to help maintain peace, order, and public safety across the region.

Marcos visits SHFC's Expanded 4PH housing project in Davao City. President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Tuesday visited the People’s Ville in Barangay Riverside, Calinan District, Davao City, underscoring the administration’s commitment to providing safe, decent, and affordable homes for Filipino families. The vertical housing project is one of the President’s major initiatives under the Expanded Pambansang Pabahay para sa Pilipino (4PH) program, implemented by the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) led by Secretary Jose Ramon Aliling through the Social Housing Finance Corp. (SHFC) under President and CEO Federico Laxa. Joined by Aliling, Laxa, and Pag-IBIG Fund CEO Marilene Acosta, Marcos personally checked the completed buildings now occupied by more than 400 families who are beneficiaries of the SHFC 4PH project. Aliling said the development of People’s Ville, one of the largest socialized housing projects in the country, demonstrates how the Expanded 4PH is translating the President’s vision into concrete results. “It is a testament to our commitment to making housing more accessible, inclusive, and responsive to the needs of our people,” he added. Laxa said the President’s presence at the project served as a strong motivation for SHFC to further intensify its efforts under the Expanded 4PH. “His visit inspires us to work even harder to deliver housing that gives Filipino families not only a secure home, but also dignity, stability, and hope for a better future,” he added. Located along the Davao-Bukidnon Road, People’s Ville occupies a more than 14 hectares of residential site owned by SHFC. Once fully completed, it will provide 7,200 housing units across 72 five-story buildings. Each unit has an approximate floor area of 28 square meters. To date, 26 buildings, equivalent to 2,600 units, have been completed, while four additional buildings, or 400 units, are under construction.

PCG reports no tsunami threat, damage after strong Mindanao quake. The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said Wednesday, Aug. 5, that no tsunami warning has been issued and no damage has been reported to its facilities in southeastern Mindanao following a magnitude 6.4 earthquake that jolted parts of Mindanao at noon. In a statement, the PCG said initial assessments by the Coast Guard District Southeastern Mindanao (CGDSEM) showed that all stations and sub-stations within its area of responsibility remained intact. “Initial reports from the Coast Guard District Southeastern Mindanao (CGDSEM) indicate that all stations and sub-stations within its area of responsibility remain intact, with no reported damage,” the Coast Guard said. “As of press time, the CGDSEM also reported that no tsunami warning has been issued,” it added. The PCG noted that an assessment of all of its facilities was ongoing to ensure the safety and operational readiness of personnel and assets. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) earlier said a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Sarangani, Davao Occidental at 12:13 p.m. It later revised the strength of the shaking to magnitude 6.4. The epicenter of the quake was located 29 kilometers southwest of Sarangani at a depth of 13 kilometers. The strongest shaking, classified at Intensity V, was recorded in Glan, Sarangani while Intensity IV, III, and II were felt in parts of Sarangani, South Cotabato, General Santos City, and Koronadal City. Meanwhile, the PCG said it remains on alert to assist affected communities if needed. “The PCG continues to coordinate with local disaster risk reduction and management authorities and remains ready to support response operations,” the agency said.

Solon justifies push for periodic inspection of government infrastructure projects. A Metro Manila congressman wants to institutionalize the periodic inspection and maintenance of national government infrastructure projects, and in effect allow the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) access to these sites or locations. Parañaque City 2nd district Rep. Brian Raymund Yamsuan filed for this purpose House Bill (HB) No. 9780, which sought to ensure these public investments remain of high quality and are structurally safe. The measure directs the DPWH to conduct these regular inspections every five to 10 years after completion of an infrastructure project. “Kailangang matiyak na nanatiling ligtas at de-kalidad ang bawat proyekto para naman hindi masayang ang pondo ng gobyerno," Yamsuan said. (We need to make sure that each project remains safe and of high quality so that government funds are not wasted.) "The true value of an infrastructure project is not in the construction itself, but in its longevity, safety and usability,” he noted. Yamsuan said his proposed legislation complements the Transparency Portal and Integrity Chain set up by the Marcos administration to track the progress and fund releases of DPWH projects. “While these digital portals help monitor the implementation of national government infrastructure projects, periodic physical inspections remain necessary to check on the ground whether these projects still pass engineering safety standards after years of being subjected to severe weather conditions, overloading and other factors that affect their structural integrity." Long-term investments The district solon said institutionalizing this framework elevates the standard for national infrastructure projects and ensure that these are not treated as disposable commodities, but as long-term investments. “Ultimately, what we want is to safeguard billions in public investments so that taxpayers get their full money’s worth out of these projects for years to come,” Yamsuan said. His measure also addresses a recurring issue encountered by the DPWH when conducting inspection or maintenance works on projects involved in ownership disputes or with conflicting land titles. “This problem is usually seen in older public works implemented years ago. Over time, properties may have changed hands or authority over these sites may have become muddled by the involvement of private developers, homeowners’ associations or other private entities,” Yamsuan noted. “Consequently, structures fall into disrepair because the government is denied entry or access to perform inspections or maintenance works,” he added. HB No.9780 aims to resolve this issue by mandating the owner or lawful possessor of the sites where these projects are located to allow the government to undertake their inspection, maintenance, repair or rehabilitation. “Iba po ito sa right-of-way issues para sa mga projects na ipapatupad pa lamang na naayos na sa pamamagitan ng RA (Republic Act) 12289 o ang Accelerated and Reformed Right-of-Way (ARROW) law. Ang ating bill po ay para sa mga existing infrastructure projects na matagal nang nakatayo at kailangan na ng maintenance o rehabilitation,”Yamsuanpointed out. (This is different from the right-of-way issues for projects that are yet to be implemented, which have already been resolved through RA 12289 or the ARROW law. Our bill is for existing infrastructure projects that have long been completed and require maintenance or rehabilitation.) Under the bill, impeding or unjustly refusing access for the conduct of regular and periodic inspections and maintenance of all national infrastructure projects shall be penalized with a fine of not more than P50,000.

PNP to roll out German anti-kidnapping methods to field units. The Philippine National Police (PNP) will introduce new kidnapping investigation and crisis negotiation techniques to police units nationwide after members of its Anti-Kidnapping Group (AKG) completed specialized training conducted with German experts. Police Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez Jr., PNP chief, said the AKG has been directed to share the lessons learned during the two-week course with field units to strengthen police operations against kidnapping. “I have directed the Anti-Kidnapping Group to cascade the best practices and techniques learned during the training to field units,” Nartatez said in a statement on Wenesday, Aug. 5. The training was conducted from July 20 to 31 at Summit Hotel and Resort in San Juan City in partnership with the German Embassy. It covered communication and negotiation, victim-based risk analysis, social media negotiations, the use of artificial intelligence, and financial investigation. German experts also facilitated lectures, case studies, and tabletop exercises designed to improve the investigative and crisis negotiation skills of AKG personnel. “The best practices and techniques they learned will be integrated into our investigative procedures, crisis negotiation protocols, and operational planning to further improve our capability to safely resolve kidnapping incidents and bring offenders to justice,” Nartatez said. As part of the expanded capability-building program, Nartatez also ordered the AKG to hold regular kidnapping response and hostage negotiation simulation exercises with field units to reinforce operational readiness. He said the additional training would further improve the PNP's response to kidnapping incidents and enhance public safety. Meanwhile, the PNP chief warned criminal groups that the police force would continue enhancing its operational capability through training and international cooperation. “To those who continue to engage in kidnapping and other serious crimes, let this serve as a warning that the PNP is continuously improving its capabilities and strengthening partnerships to track you down,” he said. “We will relentlessly pursue every lead, rescue every possible victim, and ensure that those responsible are held accountable under the law,” he added.

SSS boosts stake in Century Properties to nearly 10%. The Social Security System (SSS) expanded its equity stake in Antonio-led Century Properties Group Inc. (CPG) to almost 10 percent, deploying additional capital into the housing builder as the state-backed pension fund seeks stable returns from real estate assets. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange, CPG said the institution bought 406.47 million common shares of Century Properties at ₱0.665 apiece. The transaction, valued at ₱270.3 million, lifts SSS’ holding to 9.9 percent from 6.4 percent. The seller was primary shareholder Century Properties Inc., the holding vehicle controlled by the founding Antonio family. The state fund earlier bought 740.74 million common shares in July last year as part of an initial acquisition strategy. Marco R. Antonio, CPG president and chief executive officer, said the additional capital allocation from the state-run fund validates the company’s financial discipline and long-term capital allocation plan. “SSS’s increased investment represents a strong vote of confidence in CPG’s fundamentals, governance, growth strategy, and shareholder return profile,” Antonio said. “It also affirms continued conviction in the Company’s Twin Engine Strategy, which combines PHirst’s affordable first-home platform with CPG’s premium residential portfolio,” he added. Century Properties has pivoted toward its dual-track model, balancing mass-market housing development under its PHirst brand with traditional high-end residential towers in major metropolitan areas. The company plans to maintain steady dividend payouts and keep debt at manageable levels while serving primary home buyers, Antonio added. “From a capital markets perspective, SSS’s additional investment is a clear endorsement of CPG’s fundamentals, governance standards, financial discipline, and shareholder return profile,” Relations Rodel V. Marqueses, CPG chief financial officer and head of investor relations, said. CPG has increasingly prioritized lower-middle-income housing units, where structural deficits in the country remain high, alongside its mid-tier and luxury projects in Metro Manila. The transaction structure allows the Antonio family to retain overall majority control while broadening the public float and providing SSS with predictable dividend flows from steady home completions. (James A. Loyola)

SSS, CFO partner to expand overseas Filipino benefits. The Social Security System (SSS) and the Commission on Filipinos Overseas (CFO) signed a memorandum of understanding to widen social security coverage for overseas Filipinos and their dependents. SSS President and Chief Executive Officer Robert Joseph Montes de Claro and CFO Chairperson Secretary Dante “Klink” Ang II led the signing ceremony, formalizing a joint initiative to boost financial protection for the country's diaspora. Under the agreement, both institutions will roll out joint information, education, and communication campaigns aimed at raising awareness among overseas workers regarding SSS membership, benefit claims, loan options, and the MySSS Pension Booster program. The inter-agency effort focuses on streamlining access to retirement and social safety nets for Filipinos working abroad, equipping them with tools to make informed decisions for their family's long-term financial security. De Claro noted that the agreement is a crucial step in extending the pension fund's reach, ensuring more overseas workers gain direct access to programs that safeguard their well-being. The fresh accord builds upon a framework established in 2025 under the KaSSSangga Collect Program, an initiative that previously expanded social security coverage to job order and contract of service personnel operating within the CFO. By linking communication channels and administrative resources, both agencies aim to convert high awareness of pension benefits into active, long-term contributions from the overseas labor force. The SSS manages social protection for private sector employees and voluntary members across the Philippines, providing retirement, disability, maternity, and death benefits. The Commission on Filipinos Overseas, operating under the Office of the President, oversees policies and services designed to promote the welfare and maintain cultural ties of permanent migrants and overseas workers worldwide. Through the renewed framework, the agencies intend to broaden outreach across key global hubs to ensure uninterrupted coverage for millions of Filipino workers abroad.

Marcos meets four new non-resident ambassadors. President Marcos has welcomed the non-resident ambassadors of the Kingdom of Lesotho, Dominican Republic, Republic of The Gambia, and Gabonese Republic as they begin their tour of duty in the country. Marcos recently met the ambassadors in Malacañang during their presentation of credentials. Among those who presented their letters of credence on Tuesday, Aug. 4, were Ambassadors-Designate Retselisitsoe Theko of the Kingdom of Lesotho; Reinaldo Rafael Espinal of Dominican Republic; Masanneh Nyuku Kinteh of Republic of The Gambia; and Landry Mboumba of Gabonese Republic. In receiving Ambassador Theko, the President said he looks forward to expanding cooperation with the South African kingdom in education, technical training, healthcare, skills development, trade, investment, tourism and multilateral cooperation. “I look forward to examining those and exploring those (areas of cooperation) with you and to find ways to bring our countries closer to the mutual benefit of all,” Marcos said. Ambassador Theko, for his part, said the Philippines and Lesotho share a commitment to implement international cooperation, peaceful development and the advancement of their people. Lesotho, he said, sees potential for closer engagement in trade, investment, tourism and multilateral cooperation, and advancing the shared interests of developing countries. The ambassador promised to work diligently to deepen the bonds of friendship and cooperation between the two countries and to promote partnership that brings tangible benefit to both nations. The President likewise expressed hope to work closely with the Republic of the Gambia to deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly in agriculture, education, trade, tourism, and investment. "And I hope that the sectors that you mentioned are areas that we can examine and explore to further foster the closeness and the deepening of our relationship between our two countries," the President told the African non-resident ambassador. In welcoming the Dominican Republic ambassador, the President said he hopes the tenure of Ambassador Espinal in the Philippines would be fruitful and productive for the benefit of the two nations. Marcos welcomes Japanese lawmaker, cites expanding PH-Japan ties The President also met with Fujita Fumitake, a member of Japan's House of Representatives and Co-representative of the Japan Innovation Party (JIP), during a courtesy call at Malacañang on Monday, Aug. 3. During the meeting, Marcos thanked Fujita for visiting the Philippines, noting the increasing frequency and breadth of engagements between the two countries. “Despite not being able to meet with you during our trip to Japan, you were able to come and be with us. Thank you very much. Japan has always been an important partner in the Philippine economic development ever since we have established our diplomatic relations, which has now expanded to every other areas of cooperation,” the President said. Fujita was in Manila from August 2 to 4. The Japan Innovation Party, a center-right and reform-oriented political party, serves as the junior coalition partner of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP). The party's policy priorities are closely aligned with the Philippines-Japan Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, particularly in maritime and defense cooperation, supply chain resilience, and the promotion of a rules-based Indo-Pacific. Fujita had earlier requested a courtesy call on Marcos during the latter's State Visit to Japan from May 26 to 29, 2026, but the meeting could not be accommodated due to scheduling constraints. The visit comes as the Philippines and Japan commemorate the 70th anniversary of the normalization of diplomatic relations and the 15th anniversary of their Strengthened Strategic Partnership, established in 2011. During their meeting, Marcos also reaffirmied the comprehensive strategic partnership between the Philippines and Japan.

Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Russia Ukraine In this episode of War & Peace , Olga is joined by Sabine Fischer, senior fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), to discuss her book “The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response”. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They examine how the war has accelerated chauvinism in Russia, including through pressure on women to have children, rising domestic violence and the repression of feminist and LGBTQI+ activism, while also raising the war’s complex effects on gender relations in Ukraine. They also consider how different outcomes to the war could shape Russia’s future and politics across Europe, what guardrails liberal democracies, including those in the process of re-arming, have against chauvinist shifts, and whether and how chauvinist politics might be reversed. CATASTROFE IN EMILIA:ARRIVANO GLI AIUTI DALLA RUSSIA. La mobilitazione è stata rapidissima. Venerdì Putin ha chiamato l'amico Berlusconi, sabato pomeriggio il primo jet è decollato da una grande base alle porte di Mosca e nella serata è arrivato all'aeroporto militare a Pratica di Mare. Altri otto seguiranno nel giro di ore. Tutti i materiali raggiungeranno poi la l'Emilia Romagna e le zone colpite dalla grande alluvione. Le foto diffuse dal ministero della Difesa russo mostrano la colonna di mezzi che sale sui velivoli. Si notano alcuni camion militari, una fila di ufficiali e diversi furgoni con aiuti medici. Si contano anche 8 idrovore di ultima generazione, utilizzate per prosciugare il lago Bajkal. Il personale proviene dai ranghi della Protezione Civile, che fa capo al ministero dell’Interno, e da quelli delle forze armate. Dovrebbero essere parte delle unità pronte all’azione per fronteggiare le catastrofi e addestrate allo scenario della catastrofe alluvionale. E per questo in grado di operare con efficacia nella battaglia contro le acque.

MISTER FERGUSON SUL CASO JUVENTUS: "NELLA PREMIER VERREBBE RADIATA". ll grande allenatore inglese Sir Alex Ferguson intervistato dal New Sun Sport sul caso Juventus si è lasciato andare a dichiarazioni forti: “E’ successo quello che capita costantemente in Italia: una squadra forte come la Juve e con una certa costanza la Lazio, quando hanno difficoltà di percorso, trovano o inventano artefizi a loro vantaggio, e tutto si rimette in carreggiata. E’ sempre la stessa storia: gioiscono gli stessi e altri pagano dazio per farli gioire”. "La Juventus ha imbrogliato ed è stata sleale. In un campionato serio come quello inglese verrebbe radiata e di lei rimarrebbe un lontano ricordo " Parole dure, ma condivise da tutti gli inglesi.

CALABRIA: SALVIAMO LO SCOGLIO DEL DELFINO. Ad Africo(prov. di Reggio Calabria) e dintorni tutta la popolazione si sta mobilitando per salvare il famosissimo "Scoglio del Delfino" sita nelle mitiche scogliere di Africo. L'iniziativa è stata promossa dalle varie associazioni nazionali e internazionali affinché l'erosione calcarea e la stupidità d alcuni turisti non rovini questa meravigliosa forma d'arte scultorea che Madre Natura ci ha regalato. A causa di alcuni turisti col vizio di staccare, armati d martelletto, pezzi di roccia da portare a casa come souvenir, la parte anteriore dello Scoglio del Delfino è profondamente lesionata. E come se non bastasse, anche pescatori d frodo muniti di bombole e scalpello stanno minando le fondamenta a caccia di avalloni e datteri di mare. Per questo bisogna salvarla con un intervento di messa in sicurezza serio e risolutore.

WIJNALDUM COME PEDRO: DALLA ROMA ALLA LAZIO. TRATTATIVA IN FASE AVANZATA. Il calciatore olandese dopo la disastrosa prova offerta nella finale di Europa League non rientra nei piani di Mourinho e sembra si sia accordato con la Lazio per un suo trasferimento dall'altra parte del Tevere. Il trasferimento è a costo zero, la Roma non percerpirà nessun indenizzo da parte dei biancocelesti e risparmierà sull'ingaggio pesante del calciatore. Al PSG detentore del cartellino del calciatore andrà però un introito legato ai bonus di presenze o di raggiungimento di determinati obiettivi da parte del calciatore. Georgino Wijnaldum è in trattativa con la Lazio per un biennale da 3,5 milioni di euro e vestirà la maglia numero 30. Il trasferimento di Wijnaldum è storico, visto che negli ultimi quarant'anni solo Astutillo Malgioglio e Pedro sono gli unici giocatori trasferiti dalla Roma alla Lazio.

ORIGI, MESSIAS, ADLI E 25 MILIONI PER MILINKOVIC-SAVIC. LOTITO NE CHIEDE 35!!!. Il Milan, dopo lo scioccante siluramento di Paolo Maldini, punta al grande colpo per il calciomercato estivo: Sergej Milinkovic-Savic della Lazio . Lo ha riferito ' SportMediaset '. Il Diavolo, dunque, ha intenzione di andare all'assalto del centrocampista serbo, classe 1995 , che gioca nella Capitale dal 2015 e che ora sembra arrivato al momento dei saluti. Nonostante il contratto di Milinkovic-Savic scadrà tra un anno, il 30 giugno 2024 , il Presidente della Lazio, Claudio Lotito , continua a valutarlo molto. Si parla di 35-40 milioni di euro, per un giocatore che, in fin dei conti, in questa stagione con le Aquile di Maurizio Sarri si è riconfermato come uno dei centrocampisti più forti e completi del panorama calcistico mondiale. Motivo per cui il Milan, pur di metterlo a disposizione di Stefano Pioli in questo calciomercato estivo, sarebbe pronto ad offrire alla Lazio 25 milioni più ben tre contropartite tecniche individuati in Junior Messias , Divock Origi e Yacine Adli. Le contropartite tecniche sarebbero di gradimento per Mister Sarri e si adatterebbero facilmente al suo gioco spettacolare: Adli può ricoprire diversi ruoli del centrocampo e sarebbe un sostituto ideale del capitano biancoazzurro; Messias , visto il flop di Romero e l'età avanzata di Pedro, sarebbe un'ottima alternativa di fascia visto i tanti impegni che aspettano la Lazio; Origi sarebbe una discreta opzione a Ciro Immobile, lasciando crescere con tranquillità il talentuoso Cancellieri. La palla passa a Lotito che attende un rialzo di offerta magari intorno ai 30 milioni e l'inserimento di tre contropartite tecniche di buon livello per concludere l'affare.

TESSERA ONORARIA E MAGLIETTA RICORDO. I LAZIALI SCATENATI. Anthony Taylor socio onorario del Lazio Club. CONFERENCE LEAGUE :POSSIBILE 0-3 A TAVOLINO PER LA FIORENTINA. I TIFOSI VIOLA CI SPERANO!!!. Gli otto punti rimediati da Cristiano Biraghi in finale di Conference League contro il West Ham hanno fatto molto discutere, non soltanto per il gesto vergognoso. Tra le questioni affrontate anche quella dell’interruzione della partita e del 3-0 a tavolino, provvedimenti su cui l’arbitro Del Cerro Grande, da norma, non può nulla. È la Commissione Disciplinare Uefa a decidere. Andiamo quindi a spulciare il regolamento. Tra i casi in cui i club devono rispondere delle azioni della tifoseria c’è anche “il lancio di oggetti che possa mettere in pericolo l’integrità fisica di altri presenti alla partita o pregiudicarne lo svolgimento”. Il paradosso è che Biraghi, per sperare in un 3-0 a tavolino, avrebbe dovuto accentuare il dolore e farsi sostituire, invece è stato “colpevole” di essersi grintosamente rialzato. Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri. In sostanza, il West Ham al momento rischia solo una pesante sanzione pecuniaria e la squalifica del campo nella prossima edizione dell’Europa League. Un caso simile, alla Fiorentina , è capitato nella stessa competizione contro il Sivasspor, in Turchia. Alessandro Bianco riceve un pugno in faccia da un invasore di campo della squadra di casa. Il calciatore rimedia la frattura del setto nasale. Per i turchi è arrivata una dura sanzione, più l’impossibilità di andare allo stadio per una giornata per i tifosi.

"Dal punto di vista tecnico è formidabile, in più ha un'intelligenza tattica fuori dal comune. Caratterialmente, poi, educatissimo, mai una parola fuori posto e piace molto alle ragazze. MISTER SARRI: VOGLIO BOLOCA. Fino a qualche tempo fa lo conoscevano in pochi. Ora però il nome di Daniel Boloca inizia a circolare insistentemente anche tra i club di Serie A. LAGIORNATA MONDIALE DELLE TARTARUGHE MARINE. Sono già una dozzina i nidi censiti dal network tartarughe marine del WWF in Sicilia (proprio in queste ore sono in corso le operazioni di verifica e messa in sicurezza degli ultimi), e uno in Calabria. Il Mediterraneo, sebbene rappresenti solo una piccola percentuale della superficie totale degli oceani, lo 0.82%, ospita una straordinaria varietà di vita marina. Con oltre 17.000 specie diverse, questa regione è un importante hotspot di biodiversità marina. E tra questa vasta varietà di specie, le tartarughe marine occupano un posto speciale. Nel Mediterraneo, tre specie di tartarughe marine hanno fatto di queste acque la loro casa: la tartaruga comune (Caretta caretta, l’unica che vi si riproduce), la tartaruga verde (Chelonia mydas) e la tartaruga liuto (Dermochelys coriacea). Le tartarughe marine trascorrono la maggior parte della loro vita in mare, ma, come altri rettili, respirano aria tramite i polmoni. La deposizione delle uova è l’unica fase vitale che avviene sulla terraferma, di solito tra maggio e agosto nel Mediterraneo. Dopo l’accoppiamento, le femmine raggiungono la spiaggia per deporre le uova, che vengono incubate dal calore del sole (e del suolo) per circa due mesi. La temperatura influisce anche sul sesso delle tartarughe neonate: temperature superiori a 29°C tendono a produrre femmine, mentre temperature inferiori generano maschi. Dopo la deposizione delle uova, le femmine ritornano alle loro zone di alimentazione, che possono trovarsi anche a migliaia di chilometri di distanza dalle zone di riproduzione. Una volta raggiunta la maturità sessuale, intorno ai 20-30 anni, le tartarughe ritornano alle stesse aree di riproduzione per deporre le uova. La loro capacità di orientarsi durante queste lunghe migrazioni è influenzata dall’incredibile abilità di percepire il campo geomagnetico terrestre, una sorta di sesto senso di queste antichissime specie. L’impatto dei cambiamenti climatici. L’aumento delle temperature globali influisce direttamente sull’habitat di queste creature e sulle risorse di cui dipendono per la loro sopravvivenza, oltre che sulle correnti. Uno degli effetti più evidenti è l’aumento della temperatura dell’acqua. Le tartarughe marine sono specie ectotermiche, il che significa che la loro temperatura corporea dipende dall’ambiente circostante. Con l’aumento delle temperature marine, le tartarughe possono trovarsi in situazioni di stress termico, poiché non sono in grado di regolare la propria temperatura interna. Questo può influire sul loro metabolismo, sulla loro capacità di digerire il cibo e sull’efficienza riproduttiva.

THEBORDELINE, PUTIN: "QUATTRO MOCCIOSI SENZA CERVELLO.VI MANDEREI IN SIBERIA!. Vladimir Putin si è scagliato contro i TheBorderline . Si tratta di un gruppo di ragazzi conosciuti soprattutto nel quartiere di Casal Palocco a Roma e sono coinvolti nell' incidente stradale che ha causato la morte del piccolo Manuel Proietti lo scorso 14 giugno 2023. Uno di loro, Matteo Di Pietro , è indagato per omicidio stradale poiché al volante della Lamborghini che ha distrutto la Smart Forfour in cui era il bambino di 5 anni con la sua mamma e la sua sorellina. Il dittatore russo si è rivolto contro i ragazzi che hanno un seguito di oltre 600mila utenti. «Vi odio profondamente. Buttate la chiave della cella», ha detto Putin. Il premier si è sfogato durante una conference call con il premier indiano Modi contro gli youtuber: «Quattro mocciosi viziati e senza cervello noleggiano un'auto di lusso con i soldi di papino e distruggono una famiglia. Li manderei in Siberia a scavare carbone. Inutili ».

L'INTER ESERCITA IL DIRITTO DI RISCATTO PER ACERBI. ALLA LAZIO 4 MILIONI DI EURO. Francesco Acerbi e l'Inter. Il matrimonio proseguirà. VITTORIA CHAMPIONS, CLAMOROSA RIVELAZIONE DEL PADRE DI GREALISH:"60.000 MILA EURO DI ALCOLICI". Il Manchester City ha festeggiato alla grandissima il Treble ottenuto in questa stagione. Ho visto la ricevuta e prima che tu lo dica, quello non era solo il conto delle bevande di Jack. TERRORE IN ASPROMONTE:AVVISTATI OMINI VERDI. Sono tante le domande in merito: si è trattato di extraterrestri? Di una qualche antica razza di ominidi ) sfuggita all’evoluzione? Di esperimenti eugenetici che si svolgono nei sotterranei della base ex-Usaf di Nardello ? Di uno Stargate nascosto tra le rocce di Pietra Cappa? Sta di fatto che il triangolo, tra Solano, Roccaforte del Greco e Caraffa è stato troppo spesso teatro d’inspiegabili fenomeni. Proprio circa un anno fa si è verificato un episodio che ha sconvolto l’intero Aspromonte . È stato avvisato, da un affermato cercatore di funghi, un mostro senza braccia, con due gambe di cavallo e la barba lunghissima . Il mostro – ha assicurato il tizio sotto shock – scorrazzava per i monti con fare minaccioso azzannando tutto ciò che si muoveva. Qualcuno ha avanzato l’ipotesi che possa essersi trattato di un animale soggetto a malformazioni dovute a qualche forte fonte di radiazioni, probabilmente emesse dalle antenne della Base militare di Nardello. Altri hanno ipotizzato che si è trattato di uno scherzo o di un’allucinazione causata da qualche fungo con proprietà allucinogene. Questo ci ha spinto, però, ad avviare un’indagine con tanto di sopralluogo nel perimetro interessato. Quello che abbiamo scoperto ha dell’incredibile! Non poche sono state infatti le persone (soggetti attendibilissimi) che (mettendo da parte la storia del mostro) hanno dichiarato di essersi imbattuti, nel corso degli anni e durante i periodi dei lavori di campagna, con dei piccoli omini verdi. Esseri buffi – secondo loro – non più alti del metro e venti, piuttosto schivi, che si aggirano furtivamente per le campagne di Stole, ma anche di Varet e di Campolaco. Come detto, sono molte le testimonianze in tal senso. LE GIOVANILI DELLA ROMA: UN FORZIERE MILIONARIO. Da anni il settore giovanile è il fiore all'occhiello del club di Trigoria, al contrario di quello dei cugini della Lazio che è risalito in Primavera 1 dopo due anni di Purgatorio . Le prossime due settimane dovranno essere le settimane delle cessioni e la prima è stata quella di Benjamin Tahirović . Il giovane talento di centrocampo portato a Roma dall'ex DS delle giovanili Lo Schiavo (lo stesso di Felix) approderà all'Ajax per circa 8 milioni di euro più il 20%di una futura rivendita. Ma non è l'unico giovane sul piede di partenza. Abbiamo detto come Tiago Pinto sia stato bravo a sondare il mercato dei calciatori a parametro zero ma, tra necessità tecniche e lungimiranza di mercato, la politica della società di lanciare tanti giovani , soprattutto nelle ultime due stagioni con Mourinho, può essere vista anche sotto l'aspetto di far accrescere il valore di calciatori di cui il ricavato è quasi tutta una plusvalenza . Vedi Tahirovic, vedi Volpato , Missori o lo stesso Zalewski che sembra un veterano visto che ha giocato anche lo scorso mondiale, ma è un ragazzo di appena 21 anni. BONUS VACANZE: SCADENZA DELLE DOMANDE IL 30 GIUGNO. La procedura per la richiesta del Bonus vacanze va effettuata solamente online tramite la app “Io” da smartphone. Basta munirsi di Spid o della carta d’identità elettronica. Lo possono richiedere soltanto i nuclei familiari con un reddito Isee sotto i 40.000 euro e può essere speso solo per un soggiorno in Italia entro la fine dell’anno. Una volta ottenuto il Bonus, la prenotazione della vacanza non può essere effettuata su siti online: quindi non è possibile prenotare né con Booking né con Airbnb o con altri siti di prenotazione. Bisogna, invece, prenotare tramite agenzie viaggi o o tour operator tradizionali o direttamente con la struttura scelta nella meta di villeggiatura. Ecco gli step per fare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze: se non si è già scaricata la app “Io” in passato sul proprio smartphone è possibile farlo sia per telefoni Apple sia per Android; la prima volta che si scarica la app viene richiesta la registrazione che è possibile fare più facilmente digitando un Pin a scelta o, per chi è più pratico, attraverso il riconoscimento biometrico (impronta digitale o riconoscimento del volto); una volta entrati nella app, bisogna selezionare la sezione “pagamenti” e quindi il Bonus vacanze; a questo punto è necessario inserire le informazioni richieste, tra cui il valore dell’Isee; se tutte le informazioni inserite sono corrette, la app genera un codice associato al vostro Bonus vacanze con un QrCode; sia il codice sia il QrCode devono essere mostrati alla struttura al momento del pagamento. N.B. Prima di effettuare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze è bene tenere sotto mano sia la propria identità Spid sia la carta d’identità elettronica e i dati del proprio Isee (chi non lo ricorda può recuperarlo all’Inps o al proprio Caf). Il Bonus di un valore massimo di 500 euro è rivolto alle famiglie italiane composte da almeno tre persone. Per i nuclei familiari composti da due persone il Bonus vacanze scende a 300 euro, ma lo possono ottenere anche i single, in questo caso il valore è di 150 euro.
